Peter ,
The first fundraising reports of 2026 just dropped, and the numbers are ugly.
The RNC raised $56.1 million compared to the DNC’s $32.3 million. In March alone, the RNC nearly doubled the DNC’s haul – $21.2 million to $11.4 million.
And honestly, Peter, we get why a lot of Democrats are frustrated.
People are fired up and ready to vote, but they’re tired of being asked to give again and again, only to watch Democratic consultants burn through cash on bloated TV buys that don’t actually build the kind of turnout operation it takes to win.
That frustration is exactly why GOTV PAC started.
We built this PAC to do the work that too many campaigns skip: direct, efficient, cost-effective voter contact focused on the people most likely to be overlooked in an off-year election. Not flashy ads. Not consultant nonsense. Real turnout work.
And it works.
Last year, every single race GOTV PAC invested in on Election Day was a win. That includes the Virginia House seats that gave Democrats the exact majority that put the redistricting referendum on the ballot tomorrow.
Think about that chain of events: We won those Virginia races → those wins built the majority → that majority just gave voters the chance to cancel out Trump's Texas gerrymander and flip four Republican seats blue. None of that happens without the work we did last year!
So, Peter, will you chip in $10 right now to help us do it again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/gotvpac2026?refcode=em04202026]

You get to pick which one is crazier — Obama's strategist getting a private audience with the Pope days before three Cardinals went after Trump on 60 Minutes, or New Mexico ranking worse than California on taxes. Both happened in the last two weeks, and both are in the last two episodes of No Doubt About It.

**We’ll be back with a new show later this week, but here’s what you may have missed:**

| |
**OBAMA'S STRATEGIST MET THE POPE. THEN THE CARDINALS GOT LOUD.**

David Axelrod — who isn't Catholic — got a private audience with Pope Leo on April 9. The following Sunday, three Cardinals were on 60 Minutes, and Cardinal Cupich sounded like he was reading DNC talking points. Mark walks through the timeline and asks the question the media won't touch.

Then Archbishop Wester jumped in with an Albuquerque Journal op-ed calling Trump's response a "political cudgel." That's a bold line coming from the man who gave NM priests a very specific directive in 2022, and Mark tells the story of the priest who heard it firsthand.

Campaign strategist Jay McCluskey also joins to break down the governor's race finance reports. One Democrat has already burned through $7 million, and the other has a donor list that should end his campaign in a Democratic primary.

| |
**EPISODE 276 — NM TAXES WORSE THAN CALIFORNIA**

WalletHub put New Mexico at #4 in America for tax burden, which means only three states take more from you than we do. Mark pulled up one property tax comparison between Angel Fire and Aspen that tells the whole story, and it's not the one you'd expect.

[Then came the Eric Swalwell collapse.](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=94e069c7cf&e=567664f14c) Four women came forward, Alvin Bragg opened a probe, and even his own campaign staff put out a statement saying they were "horrified." His run for California governor didn't survive the weekend.

body:
We can’t back down now.
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107424?t=6&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF) Just a few weeks ago, Trump’s dangerous SAVE Act that would disenfranchise MILLIONS was basically a done deal.

**But thanks to Senate Democrats’ relentless fight, we’re inches away from DESTROYING this bill for good — and SAVING voting rights!**

[**We’re calling on EVERY supporter reading this to join the fight and THANK Senate Democrats for defending our democracy »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107424?t=7&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF) | [**THANK SENATE DEMOCRATS: DONATE $3 TO SIGN »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107424?t=8&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF)
---
TO: Senate Democrats
FROM: A grateful Democrat
Subject: Thank you! Dear Senate Democrats,

**Thank you for fighting TIRELESSLY against Trump’s disgusting SAVE Act that would disenfranchise married women, target poll workers, and destroy vote-by-mail.**

This is true heroism — and exactly the kind of leadership we need to defeat Republicans’ disgusting attacks on the American people!

It’s clear: Trump wouldn’t be doing this if he wasn’t TERRIFIED. He KNOWS Democrats are on track to end his MAGA trifecta in November.

**He’ll do everything in his power to silence our votes, but with a strong grassroots coalition on our side, I know we can stop him.**

[**So I'm signing this letter and donating $3 to the Voter Protection Project to THANK YOU for putting it all on the line to save our country and to help FLIP the majorities this November! »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107424?t=9&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF) | [**RUSH $3 TO SIGN ON BEFORE WE CLOSE THIS LETTER AT MIDNIGHT »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/107424?t=10&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF)

**_X A grateful Democrat_**
—The Voter Protection Project
878179

(www.protectvoting.org)
Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. 401 2nd Ave. S, Ste. 303, Seattle, WA 98104

Please, consider making a [one-time contribution by clicking here](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/121?t=1&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF). **Or, to make the most powerful lasting impact and help us oust Republicans up and down the ballot who attack our right to vote, make a[monthly sustaining contribution by clicking here](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/122?t=2&akid=23767%2E878179%2E9lV3SF).**

| Dear Peter,
Are you excited for this weekend? Because it just got even bigger. Convention 2026 has officially leveled up!
On behalf of the full team and leadership at MassGOP, I am beyond excited to announce that Seth Dillon, CEO of The Babylon Bee, will take the stage as our 2026 Republican Nominating Convention keynote speaker!
With razor-sharp wit and fearless commentary, Seth has built a cultural phenomenon that cuts through the noise by saying what others won't. Under his leadership, The Babylon Bee has become a powerhouse voice in media, using satire to expose truth and challenge the status quo.
But Seth isn't just entertaining, he's on the front lines. From censorship battles to high-profile deplatforming fights, he has emerged as a leading advocate for free speech in America. His message is bold, timely, and guaranteed to energize anyone who cares about the future of open dialogue.
Whether on college campuses or national stages, Seth delivers a keynote that challenges, provokes, and inspires. And, he'll keep you laughing.
This is one you do not want to miss.
Join us for an unforgettable convention experience as we hear from one of the most dynamic voices in media today.
I promise you: Convention 2026 will be one to remember.
Cheers!
Haley Jones Executive Director Massachusetts Republican Party

## Iran Ceasefire Set to Expire Today
President Trump on Monday said the ceasefire with Iran is "highly unlikely" to be extended, warning that if it expires Tuesday evening, "then lots of bombs start going off." The two-week truce has held since April 7, but [tensions have escalated](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAURL9GMyxARA0INjGbTTe07sBlvDsIFjLDzn79K98vvLCrq7rrnD-39QYUKD5-w46m-LRGrGfAUjCvFuFETxkdggsUMWKF4wi4Si4144pJsTqg8FlV64xHlNi3aMQ46lFrwUW7GdGPs3R3xbWeQerBwwjzqCav-x713bdkrjWupBCcT2LqhmGYvO2VtZO3bhaN4uiopNz9TRTLhj580htzZ9PeBrOVcpxN_6uRSyOXWmvn07-L4uobuQR6I7tyI5fXyShDZBUy21LeX__ZPST7BIfsgCedBSKDI1NgkrfZuKNSCHTqsVH8sQOF79PyI1NvI78CAAD__y-Qfg0) sharply in recent days. The U.S. Navy on Sunday fired on and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship, the _Touska_ , in the Gulf of Oman after the vessel ignored six hours of warnings. [Watch a video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu8yAUBeCnwVssuGADA8O_eMu_dkQELsmtiHFtFJQ-feW-QrcjHemTzvm4-mugQuv9f3iia7n6FftRsDXcfcRwYKYdE4ZUaMUVe9i2gh44zBeuLiB8ClTeXg3JZURAOaATWs96ngUXw8MJayUaUAaTDgGUyNNNSZOt0hCTjQO5U-MKhODcCDNO02RylCpGk2OygimOiVrdx89Ka3tgLu_6wn2M9TkU92htO5j8x2BhsPTex9stnh2D5RzDYHlRwnqGKLvkZf76VrYOu0tbp1LomDVT_P4MVH7N9qcjXg5-AgAA__8exnC5). Iran's military called the seizure "armed piracy" and vowed retaliation, saying Washington violated the ceasefire. A U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance, envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner was heading to Islamabad on Monday for another round of talks, but Iran's foreign ministry said it has [no plans to negotiate](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtSAUhJ8GOwwgoreg-Bu7-7dbmnPhoGeDaIC9xrffeF9hu8lMMpn5vp7zEyhSWv7DhraGfU54loi1Yp4dQsFAGT2Cj5Qw4QnHEXFWQhkuNFdy9kDxmnXjbUBU2DVo5TCYwRgpZLNaAWNwr0GKXguQnTcPHYYO-957o7sADdm7TWglpRCjHNu-78fgOu3cGJx_SKYFeqp7br93SnXFEK_9jbl1-9ZEu9Z6FNb9Y2piajrPs3Wvcr-4c6amWzI11fyzHXzDUmChtHDKkDiEipmvyAuQ5xXXj7lkRM_rzvGN-aorpYWpqcnWHyfFSMUMTItlA4qfDfVP4N5W_QYAAP__NK2EAg), accusing the U.S. of lacking seriousness. Trump told reporters the administration's demand is simple: _"No nuclear weapons. Very simple. Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon."_ No tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday.
## Most Common US Surnames Little Changed in Two Centuries
America's 15 most common last names [continue to be dominated](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uxCAUBODT4M4WPOOfLSjSuNu0KS0Mj_WLMFhAFvn20WaPkG6amU-ar_t61-QpPD71gaq4uAas2WMpmFaDOqOjhBa19RQwYNXn6XEFDmPLZQtitZr8tcrGKocI2DeoxDSN0zgKLppdDTc5DP3keO_MdtvQbk5otNxI2RucoCH1WuMShOB8FnM3DMPsTC-NmZ2xN8EkR0slpu47Uig7On_FJ6bOxKPxai_lzKz_YLAwWGqtncGQf3L3iE8Gi6ct6XQxWHKJiTAzWF4gg4XLd-btu9EGfWBurS6628vhm6TsWcl7yuPEJH8cmvyfWv511VPBbwAAAP__OBN8jg) by surnames such as Smith and Johnson, though they've been joined this century by six predominantly Hispanic last names: Garcia, Gonzalez, Hernandez, Lopez, Martinez, and Rodriguez. Eight English and Welsh-origin surnames--Smith, Johnson, Williams, Brown, Jones, Miller, Davis, and Wilson--[have held top-15 spots](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3SAQhZ8Gd1wB_t3CRaTI3aZNac3CYSHCYMFovfftI988QsqZT-fo0_n9vr9TTDF__qIDK_uyZ1wtgRl1t6AGHyscyKWYkXHReSbsRplJqkEavTuK6bkPnVs9YNB3WPU8T_M0aaW7sLrpzYH6-UNZTctivXGayAxqpIG0QhfXu00NRmulFr08xnFcvO0Haxdv3ZsWg4KLXOrjT4mZA3x6li_Uhy1Hl9bAfDbR_xBmE2bjgBBTupkwWyjHLd2E2TK-G1PdD7hI-xUrhNnGpR9HPcmjNJbFSw6QmTiW3CSXU2Y60CRVvEijA7LFbP-delaqSXxbnHw_GuQsORC_AhnXbdRv_FHhRf8znF1d3XnFlGKbZjGoz4Piy7Tj_5r-azV_AwAA__-COZmN) continuously since the first census in 1790, despite an 84-fold increase in population. The release also included first-name data for the first time since 1990. The five most common first names, Michael, John, James, David, and Robert, [were all traditionally male](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OwyAQBOCnwR0RbPBfQXGNu1x7pYXZJdkTBssQW3n7U_IKV45GGn2an9t8cxw53b_dSraGPCc6S6RaaZ89uUKBd0JyGDlRotNtW6QZFHRSGQl6RsfxNZsGbSACujZkdd93fddppZuHxX5oW2VGBQFBG1ywD-PoUC_dsowtNGzfa8qA1koNeri0bTsEfzXeD8HjqIVRhFzzfvnNnOqDQnzlg_aLz2sT7aPWrYjrl4BJwPThHJk9vWsB04oCpvgsy-sdcqnS53XNSQbeS5XRlSqTW6nInQ5ykVBykolO-SzSUyrPItFVJ2BqdovbyTFy6Xph1H11HD-K-q_rDgt_AQAA____1IRC) because men share popular names at roughly twice the rate women do.
## Red Lobster's 'Endless Shrimp' Returns Despite Bankruptcy

# $572 Million and
# West Virginia Gets Nothing!

---
|
---
|
---
| |
Dear Friend,

Let’s talk about the MARL transmission line.
Senator Shelley Moore Capito supports it.
You’re paying for it.
And West Virginia gets nothing.
Latest estimates show [**West Virginia customers will be stuck covering $572 million**](https://tomwillis.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3634ddeac3944e116590ee972&id=5565c2229c&e=a0285cc040) — more than three times the original projection — for a project that delivers little to no benefit to our state.
**Half a billion dollars.**
**Out of your pocket.**
**For someone else’s gain.**
So why would she support it?
**Follow the money.**
The same energy companies behind MARL have lobbyists and influence in Washington.
And once again, West Virginia families come last.
Shelley Moore Capito has lost her way — and West Virginia is the one paying for it.
That’s exactly why I’m running for the U.S. Senate.
I’ve spent 26 years serving this country as a Green Beret.
I’ve built a business here in West Virginia.
I’ve served in the State Senate, fighting for our people.
And I’ve seen what happens when politicians lose their way.
They stop fighting for you —
And start taking care of themselves.
**I oppose the MARL transmission line. Period.**
**I didn’t just say it — I took action.**
I hand-drafted language in Senate Bill 669 that would have stopped projects like MARL by requiring one simple standard:
**If it doesn’t benefit West Virginia by at least 51% — it doesn’t get approved.**
No loopholes.No backroom deals.
No selling out our state.
But it was killed in the House.
Notably, my former opponent, Craig Blair, is now lobbying in Charleston for NextEra and the MARL project.
**Same insiders. Same outcome.**
Why?
**Follow the money.**
Meanwhile, West Virginia families are stuck paying the bill.
That’s not who we are.
**We’re hardworking people.**
We believe in faith, family, and taking care of each other.
And we deserve leaders who do the same.
Not politicians who sell us out.
I’m running because it’s time to put West Virginia first again.
If you’re tired of being ignored...
If you’re tired of footing the bill for their deals...
If you’re ready to hold them accountable...
Then don’t sit this one out.
**Vote Tom Willis on May 12.**
**IT’S TIME FOR A CHANGE WV!**

**Tom Willis**

## Landowners Face Deadline to Oppose Power Line
Residents of 11 counties have until Monday to [intervene](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFygzAQRL8GOjE6CUumUJGGzmlTMgc6jDIyx0iywX-fwb-Qfmff7vu5DTcMMaz3b3yQK8fMw0p7jlQKpSHxyAWPQMeGq88zJYwL3zMOSiojZCsUDB5DfA9t7d0ofQc1ObDWWNNpgHpxGrQZ4XrtyKjLrO1FI9jRjOjtpCcc6-DOMtkqAJBwgaaTNLfaSNPJDohs1UryoXBqykKFDsxzfPOLUjPxo45uKWXLlf6qVF-pft_3ZubD4jOXsJ6RSvXnp0r1VvAq3vxMIgdPgteJk9h4pyRiWElsiX9pKiJjRM_iw6qT89seYgzZnFPuDwzxQy7_8_Vy6i8AAP__04iBGQ) in an application to build a 765-kilovolt transmission line from Bell County to Schleicher. The project is one of several authorized by lawmakers in 2023 to meet the rising power demand of data centers and the oil and gas industry in West Texas. Since 1982, Pennsylvania's Medicaid recipients have been denied abortion coverage -- for over four decades, low-income women have been shut out of reproductive care.
Yesterday, that changed.
Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Court struck down the ban, ruling it unconstitutional. More than that, the Commonwealth Court found that the right to abortion is fundamental. This is HUGE--and YOU helped make it happen.

Because you stepped up, women across Pennsylvania will finally get the care they deserve. Because of you, the rights of women in PA have been expanded. On their behalf--thank you.
But this didn't happen by chance.
In 2025, Defend Our Courts built a full-scale electoral program targeting 750,000 low-propensity Democratic voters. We doubled turnout from 30% to 60%--driving hundreds of thousands of additional votes in a judicial election most people ignore.
Those voters didn't just retain Supreme Court Justices Donohue, Dougherty, and Wecht.They also helped retain Judge Wojcik and elect Judge Stella Tsai to the Commonwealth Court.
Those are the judges who made yesterday's ruling possible. That's your impact.
And when opponents appeal this decision to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, as they will, the pro-rights majority you helped protect will be there to uphold it.
But we don't get to stop here. Because while Pennsylvania women are gaining rights--
Women in Georgia are still losing them.

---

# A Closer Look at Recent Measles Data
|
---
|
---
| Last week, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services released the graphic below showing **global measles cases** from the past year. While the data clearly shows that the U.S. has a significantly lower per capita rate than other large regions, some commentary has attempted to **blame HHS Secretary Kennedy** for measles cases in the United States. That claim deserves a closer look. The idea that measles was “eliminated” in 2000 (and that current cases represent a reversal due to declining vaccination rates) is often based on a **misunderstanding of the term “elimination.”** The U.S. still maintains measles elimination status as defined by the World Health Organization, but this **does not mean zero cases.** In public health, “elimination” refers to the absence of sustained domestic transmission for 12 months or more, not the absence of all cases. It also does not mean isolated or imported cases will never occur. _In fact, according to the CDC, the U.S. has never had a full year with zero measles cases._ Public concern around measles has, at times, influenced policy decisions at the state level, including efforts to expand vaccine mandates or limit exemptions. Given the presence of vaccine-strain and wild-type infections, as well as non-responders (individuals who do not mount an immune response to vaccination), **history indicates that some cases will continue to occur each year.** Staying proactive about personal and public health is important, but so is ensuring that policy decisions are guided by **accurate information rather than fear-driven narratives** , something the mandates of the COVID era clearly demonstrated.

clean_body: | | Plus our monthly poll, volunteer opportunities & more! | | | | | | A Closer Look at Recent Measles Data | | | Last week, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services released the graphic below showing global measles cases from the past year. While the data clearly shows that the U.S. has a significantly lower per capita rate than other large regions, some commentary has attempted to blame HHS Secretary Kennedy for measles cases in the United States. That claim deserves a closer look. The idea that measles was “eliminated” in 2000 (and that current cases represent a reversal due to declining vaccination rates) is often based on a misunderstanding of the term “elimination.” The U.S. still maintains measles elimination status as defined by the World Health Organization, but this does not mean zero cases. In public health, “elimination” refers to the absence of sustained domestic transmission for 12 months or more, not the absence of all cases. It also does not mean isolated or imported cases will never occur. In fact, according to the CDC, the U.S. has never had a full year with zero measles cases. Public concern around measles has, at times, influenced policy decisions at the state level, including efforts to expand vaccine mandates or limit exemptions. Given the presence of vaccine-strain and wild-type infections, as well as non-responders (individuals who do not mount an immune response to vaccination), history indicates that some cases will continue to occur each year. Staying proactive about personal and public health is important, but so is ensuring that policy decisions are guided by accurate information rather than fear-driven narratives , something the mandates of the COVID era clearly demonstrated. | | | Vax Views | | | | | | Sound off! | Modern fear-based depictions of measles contrast sharply with mid-century TV, books, and comics that often treated (or even joked about) it as a harmless childhood rite of passage. | | **Ban Non-Citizen Voting!**
---
Dear Fellow Patriot, **[I’m writing today because our “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition Drive must be supercharged immediately.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2l127po0ci6l1vvmlpefvm2iqf9vp4606afg2tg_rp22sh2s8i6epr3ctge9o36cdh2bs)** And at a moment like this, we are reaching out to Americans who still believe in election integrity, the Constitution, and the fundamental principle that **only citizens should decide our elections.** If you’ve ever heard of **AMAC Action** , you know that we are one of the nation’s leading conservative advocacy organizations—mobilizing millions of Americans to stand up for limited government, secure elections, and the values that made this country great.Right now, we need your voice. **[Please click here to submit your signed “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” petition in the next 48 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zr1445slflr0frffag2btsq8950g520j70om207g_rp22sh2s8i6epr3ctge9o36cdh2bs)** My friend, you know that with razor-thin margins in the House and Senate, all bets are off after the midterm elections. That means we must act **now** , while we still have the opportunity.We must **BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING** before it’s too late.Today, millions of illegal immigrants who entered the country are being counted in ways that directly impact political power.And that means:
---
* More congressional seats for states with large illegal populations
* More Electoral College votes
* More federal funding
* More political power

---
And more opportunity for non-citizens to end up on voter rolls.That’s exactly why AMAC Action launched this national petition drive.So far, **more than 100,000 petitions** have already been signed by concerned Americans.But it is not enough.**[To force action—to apply real pressure—we must reach 500,000 signed petitions.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zcghvr799v4ldl6cpjq0gh8f4qs4542um06r40e0_rp22sh2s8i6epr3ctge9o36cdh2bs)****Half a million.** That’s the kind of number that gets politicians’ attention.But without your signature, we won’t get there in time.To stop non-citizen voting, concerned citizens across the country must send one loud and unmistakable message:
---
1. **Only American citizens should be counted in the census.**
2. **Only American citizens should have a vote.**

---
[ ** Sign the Petition** ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zagtdndoivqgu28gjhnnnntaanveqo2ul5lk6f78_rp22sh2s8i6epr3ctge9o36cdh2bs)
---
You’re receiving this message because you’ve been identified as someone who may be willing to take a stand on critical issues like this. And at a moment like this, every signature matters. Because without action, momentum is lost—and we cannot afford to lose momentum with the midterms approaching.When you sign and submit your petition in the next 48 hours with your petition sponsorship gift you will help AMAC Action:
---
* Distribute hundreds of thousands of additional petitions by mail, email, text, and social media
* Expand digital outreach to recruit more conservative seniors
* Organize state-level petition drives
* Deliver signed petitions directly to lawmakers
* Push election integrity legislation that safeguards your vote
* Fight for census reform so representation reflects citizens only

---
That’s a lot to accomplish.But we’ve seen what’s possible when Americans step forward.With the help of patriots just like you, we’ve already helped:
---
* Pass the Rescissions Act to cut wasteful spending
* Push the “One Big, Beautiful Bill” across the finish line
* Advance the SAVE Act in the House

---
And so much more. But now, we must finish the job. Stopping non-citizen voting is one of the most common-sense issues of our time. And if enough Americans take action—we can get it done.Some have chosen to ignore this issue. The Left is counting on that. But millions of Americans are taking action. We hope you will be one of them. **[Please sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” petition and submit it within the next 48 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z45k6u1lsf3muq7v0gtbe94ra75r99hcegem2398_rp22sh2s8i6epr3ctge9o36cdh2bs)**
---

**Rebecca Weber,_Chairwoman_****AMAC Action**

Peter,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**
---
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=b79a1d43f8564c62a0eb36f2a1810967&_e=NcRoJ5wCq4ATyBwPdLpG_ng5PjBTk87Oc9NPaO0IG7AB0waNGRnbDWOdO5HiOBMtBMsiLWHe2K1tduOa1EOh-d05NZ9WMnGo-5xG86dhG5TddcHvoU4zV4k1OLysPSkaGkphTK1u8xlWFfeWL0JoXJ5i_hXZBgJnjbLAv_PrZRwGiBfzHMJk2LBbdFx9iA5bDUjMPImCH9ww3UmgW8WUNQPCcum_JljaDNWL_wCfAvNx6QyO2ixAAtv_MiGRofR3xWKl1HlKzm06PeQaLmsjmkR0gMBymZGsOwSywchIBud9ZoDJXmRjuBoLtkbvxlfg-w2_LGjIQYQxB-mRhJsWSWvY_jOwC5sbs-IUJpflggvbzUBDYqUyz_xdkbIs8CL4njnSFJnEtE2msa66thLQObAqd7_C4pZoW7yoyTDYAehn60HPd32-sOF37yB0JrLBEN2TBpKlVTqJwnF5sDxcCtA2BiZrQTwHPpy33YIpP4Q62rOafNKBMGSW9vEFKncnrFLnOUUhwSBY3OdIyJvBulsDJe4TwxnBIsvOB9NwoU1xF5b1ECoHT_w6sU6_EToCNZAXuGfmwqT6N4j3OuviuFM-QbQCtc9Edtgh1PG9rhpgrBzs0RibjJVR4zZ6MMu7UvqzWzb5sMUY0bVAZm3i4sLdOZeRn3BXuQK6vcpKHjymp9yJOssj9C8sQHNQJEt8)

You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. * Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Joining me is John Ferguson a drone expert and the Founder and Chairman of Saxon Aerospace and Saxon Unmanned, a Kansas based manufacturer of long range, military grade unmanned aircraft and remote systems.

"Last year, when residents up and down the East Coast reported mysterious drones appearing night after night, it was John Ferguson's expertise that helped major news outlets connect the dots. His analysis led to national reporting -- including Newsweek's coverage titled Mystery Drones Could Be Trying to Find 'Radioactive Material' citing Ferguson as the aerospace CEO explaining the technology behind those detection flights." John also appeared on Patrick Bet David and Joe Rogan picked up the story.

Ferguson, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and former reconnaissance scout swimmer, went on to become a deep sea diver, submersible vehicle pilot, and global infrastructure specialist, working in more than 80 countries. Ferguson holds multiple pending U.S. patents and is known for designing rugged, life saving, cost saving technologies relied on by major clients worldwide including the military, energy, and agriculture sectors. For more about John visit
https://saxonunmanned.com

subject: We’re taking the Trump administration to court
body:
---
Derek — it’s Andie Levien here with an update on our lawsuit against the Trump administration. The DNC is suing to block Trump’s executive order that would restrict voting-by-mail by giving the Department of Homeland Security _unprecedented and unlawful_ oversight over who can vote. The unfortunate truth is that we have a narrow window to act, which is why we need your help right now. [**Please chip in $7 today to help power our fight. Your donation will be put to work immediately to help us shape the future of voting rights in America.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?refcode=em_20260421_6808_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6808_22930333_1s6wXI&akid=6808%2E22930333%2E1s6wXI) **[CHIP IN $7 TO HELP US FIGHT BACK](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?refcode=em_20260421_6808_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6808_22930333_1s6wXI&akid=6808%2E22930333%2E1s6wXI)** If you’re skeptical about how your donation can help, please, let me explain:
* Last year, Trump signed an executive order that could have disenfranchised married women who changed their names and members of the armed services. We sued, this grassroots team rallied behind us, and **we won in court.**
* Since then, Trump has sought to “take over” state-run elections, he’s used the FBI to _seize ballots_ from election offices in Georgia, and he’s tried to coerce states into giving him access to their voter rolls.
* Now, he’s taking it to a new level: His new executive order directs the federal government to build a voter list for each state to decide who can and cannot vote by mail— and he’s told the Postal Service to refuse to carry ballots for anyone not on their list.

Derek, I want to tell you directly that _**the DNC won’t let this happen._** With the help of grassroots supporters like _you_ , we’ll block his order from going into effect. [**We’ll defend your right to vote. We’ll protect your right to free and fair elections. And, when November rolls around, we’ll make sure Democrats can kick these aspiring authoritarians out of office. I hope you’re with me, and I hope you’ll consider chipping in $7 or any amount you can spare right now to help us fight back.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?refcode=em_20260421_6808_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6808_22930333_1s6wXI&akid=6808%2E22930333%2E1s6wXI) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-april-2026?express_lane=true&amount=7&refcode=em_20260421_6808_fr&refcode2=6808_22930333_1s6wXI&akid=6808%2E22930333%2E1s6wXI)**

| When it rains, it pours, it’s no exaggeration to say that we’re up against a lot of far-right money. MAGA dark money is flowing into Wisconsin **[will you rush $15 to help our campaign compete with their warchest?](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-apr26.K8_u48&amount=15&refcode=MB_EM_FR_042126_B1_Against&t=2&akid=6067%2E196590%2E4YhWFD)** [****](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-apr26.K8_u48&amount=15&refcode=MB_EM_FR_042126_B1_Against&t=3&akid=6067%2E196590%2E4YhWFD)**Here’s what his ads won’t tell you:** Our farmers continue struggling, and Tiffany is pushing policies that only make it worse. **Like staunchly defending tariffs** , which sparked a trade war that’s left farmers hurting. An anti-billionaire organization is endorsing a billionaire, and I don't know how you're supposed to take that seriously without calling it exactly what it is. Hypocrisy!
[Our Revolution](https://substack.com/redirect/506c6837-4ec3-42de-a8cc-6846452831dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the group built by Bernie Sanders around fighting the billionaire class and getting money out of politics, just endorsed Tom Steyer, a billionaire who is pouring hundreds of millions of dollars of his own money into a race. That's the exact behavior they've spent years saying is the problem.
[| | | | | Our Revolution
---
@OurRevolution
We've never endorsed a billionaire -- but Tom Steyer is using his position to upset the system. As Our Revolution executive director Joseph Geevarghese told @theintercept , "he's been a partner in the movement. Most billionaires have used their wealth and privilege to lock in the
| 4:43 PM * Apr 20, 2026 * 41.8K Views110 Replies * 124 Reposts * 690 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/fd289447-408d-4126-98d5-6fe1c0c441da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And what makes it worse is that they don't even try to reconcile it in a serious way. The justification is that he is "upsetting the system" and that he has the best chance to stop Republicans. But if you actually think about that for more than a second, it falls apart. Spending hundreds of millions of dollars to influence an election is not upsetting the system, it is the system. It's the very thing they claim to be fighting against, just now it's happening in a way that benefits them.
[| | | | | Chanteezy! ♉️💛
---
@iamchanteezy
Our Revolution endorsing Tom Steyer (a Billionaire) for Governor of California proves they ain't about progressive policies at all.
| 2:35 AM * Apr 21, 2026 * 5.41K Views21 Replies * 102 Reposts * 340 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/01a2a47f-d8db-463c-b1c9-d725cb9c7d46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## This IS the Pattern
What bothers me about this is not just the decision is that we have seen this movie before.
The Democratic Party sets these very clear moral positions, they build messaging around them, they rally people around them, and then the second those positions get in the way of winning, they abandon them.
You see it over and over again.
They talk about protecting democracy and then avoid real primary competition when it becomes inconvenient.
They talk about banning stock trading in Congress, and then you have situations like Ro Khanna pushing a ban while his household is actively trading millions of dollars.
They talk about getting money out of politics, and then justify massive spending when it's on their side.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/47c54459-84bd-471a-85e7-7c367c8fbe71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And every time, the explanation is the same. They'll tell you they have to win. That the stakes are too high. That this is different. That this is necessary. But it completely undermines everything they were saying before.
Do they think we are dumb?
* * *
## The "Good Billionaire" Problem
What this really exposes is the idea that there are good billionaires and bad billionaires, depending on who they support.
The bad billionaires are the oligarchs, the corrupting influence, the people buying elections.
**But the good billionaires are the ones that are doing the exact same thing but for our side**.
You see names like Steyer, J. B. Pritzker, George Soros, and Reid Hoffman get treated as exceptions, not because the principle changed, but because it is the **blue** team.
If your position is that money in politics is corrupting the system, then it doesn't suddenly become less corrupting because it's helping your side. Either the principle matters or it doesn't. You don't get to redefine it every time the bag is making it rain for your team.
* * *
This is the part that I think people are actually reacting to, even if they don't always articulate it this way.
It's not just the hypocrisy. It's the fact that they think nobody notices.
They really think we are dumb.

You can't spend years telling people that money in politics is the root of the problem, that billionaires are distorting democracy, and then turn around and say this time it's fine because it helps you win. You can't say you want ethical standards and then immediately carve out exceptions when it benefits you.
At some point, people stop taking that seriously. Not because they don't agree with the original goal, but because they don't believe you actually stand by it.
And that's where this becomes a bigger problem than just one endorsement. It erodes credibility. It makes everything sound like bullshit.
* * *
## Stand on Business
At the end of the day, this isn't about whether you support Steyer or oppose him. It's about whether the things you say actually mean anything.
If the goal is just to win, then say that. Say you're going to use whatever tools are available and stop pretending it's about principle. But if you're going to take a moral stance, if you're going to build an entire movement around that stance, then you have to stick to it!
Because right now, we look like fucking dumb hypocrites. And, people are paying attention to that.

Make It Make Sense | | | Apr 21 | | | | | | | | | | | | An anti-billionaire organization is endorsing a billionaire, and I don't know how you're supposed to take that seriously without calling it exactly what it is. Hypocrisy! , the group built by Bernie Sanders around fighting the billionaire class and getting money out of politics, just endorsed Tom Steyer, a billionaire who is pouring hundreds of millions of dollars of his own money into a race. That's the exact behavior they've spent years saying is the problem. And what makes it worse is that they don't even try to reconcile it in a serious way. The justification is that he is "upsetting the system" and that he has the best chance to stop Republicans. But if you actually think about that for more than a second, it falls apart. Spending hundreds of millions of dollars to influence an election is not upsetting the system, it is the system. It's the very thing they claim to be fighting against, just now it's happening in a way that benefits them. This IS the Pattern What bothers me about this is not just the decision is that we have seen this movie before. The Democratic Party sets these very clear moral positions, they build messaging around them, they rally people around them, and then the second those positions get in the way of winning, they abandon them. You see it over and over again. They talk about protecting democracy and then avoid real primary competition when it becomes inconvenient. They talk about banning stock trading in Congress, and then you have situations like Ro Khanna pushing a ban while his household is actively trading millions of dollars. They talk about getting money out of politics, and then justify massive spending when it's on their side. And every time, the explanation is the same. They'll tell you they have to win. That the stakes are too high. That this is different. That this is necessary. But it completely undermines everything they were saying before. Do they think we are dumb? The "Good Billionaire" Problem What this really exposes is the idea that there are good billionaires and bad billionaires, depending on who they support. The bad billionaires are the oligarchs, the corrupting influence, the people buying elections. But the good billionaires are the ones that are doing the exact same thing but for our side. You see names like Steyer, J. B. Pritzker, George Soros, and Reid Hoffman get treated as exceptions, not because the principle changed, but because it is the blue team. If your position is that money in politics is corrupting the system, then it doesn't suddenly become less corrupting because it's helping your side. Either the principle matters or it doesn't. You don't get to redefine it every time the bag is making it rain for your team. This is the part that I think people are actually reacting to, even if they don't always articulate it this way. It's not just the hypocrisy. It's the fact that they think nobody notices. They really think we are dumb. You can't spend years telling people that money in politics is the root of the problem, that billionaires are distorting democracy, and then turn around and say this time it's fine because it helps you win. You can't say you want ethical standards and then immediately carve out exceptions when it benefits you. At some point, people stop taking that seriously. Not because they don't agree with the original goal, but because they don't believe you actually stand by it. And that's where this becomes a bigger problem than just one endorsement. It erodes credibility. It makes everything sound like bullshit. Stand on Business At the end of the day, this isn't about whether you support Steyer or oppose him. It's about whether the things you say actually mean anything. If the goal is just to win, then say that. Say you're going to use whatever tools are available and stop pretending it's about principle. But if you're going to take a moral stance, if you're going to build an entire movement around that stance, then you have to stick to it! Because right now, we look like fucking dumb hypocrites. And, people are paying attention to that. Stay Angry Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by support Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

### China's Organ Harvesting Industry
---
| |
---
| | It sounds like the plot of a horror film — healthy people killed so that sick people can have their organs. But what if it isn't fiction? What if it's happening right now, on an industrial scale, and people from around the world are quietly flying to China to benefit from it? This is the unsettling reality that journalist and author Jan Jekielek has spent years investigating — and the findings are as disturbing as they are urgent. Jekielek, a senior editor at the Epoch Times and host of the acclaimed interview series American Thought Leaders, has built a reputation for tackling stories that others won't touch. His latest work, Killed to Order — a New York Times bestseller — pulls back the curtain on China's organ transplant industry and the global phenomenon known as "transplant tourism," in which patients travel abroad to receive organs with suspiciously short waiting times. It's a conversation worth having — and we think you'll find it hard to stop listening. Tune in to the full episode on: [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/16PsSh13J/c?w=AV3GAXf3y5w145LUhHRvsxSxHZjnASWKpXBuPHDqJEA.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vQE1vbXNmb3JBbWVyaWNhIiwiciI6ImE2YmQ0MDVhLTJhMDUtNGE3Ny1hZDgzLTFmZTI1OGYzMWI4MCIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/16PsSh13J/c?w=wXS23wZ6KNd7gchDlNEca1WnZR8NJJFfS4EHBlegOig.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ydW1ibGUuY29tL2MvYy0xMjA2NzMzP2U5cz1zcmNfdjFfY2JsIiwiciI6ImE2YmQ0MDVhLTJhMDUtNGE3Ny1hZDgzLTFmZTI1OGYzMWI4MCIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/16PsSh13J/c?w=TON0WJDto5TRX1T4syRyrP-moMN65vY5EGD1-ug-61E.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL3Nob3cvMHBIemFBWGJCRVVFUlBxajluQlhxYyIsInIiOiJhNmJkNDA1YS0yYTA1LTRhNzctYWQ4My0xZmUyNThmMzFiODAiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiI0YWEzZmM0My1kYjVlLTQxNjYtOWJjMi1kN2RmYjcyZDcyMTQifQ) or [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/16PsSh13J/c?w=vVvHepcslCL6t2JFiVf6errCg2YXXLjlH0mkK2pMozw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9wb2RjYXN0cy5hcHBsZS5jb20vdXMvcG9kY2FzdC9tb21zLWZvci1hbWVyaWNhLXBvZGNhc3QvaWQxNjE2OTIwMTIxIiwiciI6ImE2YmQ0MDVhLTJhMDUtNGE3Ny1hZDgzLTFmZTI1OGYzMWI4MCIsIm0iOiJtYWlsIiwiYyI6IjRhYTNmYzQzLWRiNWUtNDE2Ni05YmMyLWQ3ZGZiNzJkNzIxNCJ9).

# Why Embracing Life in America Will Always Beat a Culture of Death
---
| |
---
| | Across America, a profound struggle exists—between a culture that protects life and one that diminishes its worth. Deep ideological divides shape this moment, as debates over human dignity, identity, and the value of life rage. Yet even amid cultural tensions, signs of hope are emerging. A new generation is rediscovering faith, embracing purpose, and recognizing the inherent worth of every human life. Patriotism is rising once again, and with it, a renewed commitment to life and liberty. Life is sacred. God fashioned it as the essence of growth and flourishing on our big blue ball. And for those of us who are believers in Jesus, we know the promise of an unending, rich life beyond the grave. Life is of inestimable value – and for it, we express due gratitude to the Giver of all life – our faithful Creator. With all of that, it’s hard to understand the culture of death that has spread across our nation like a black mold – choking the life out of our children, youth, and so many others. It's a question worth sitting with. To read the full blog and continue the conversation — join our free membership at Moms TownSquare.

Friend,
What are we doing here?

subject: Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin
body:
Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-kqs1grv7ud-12933535?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
# Property Tax Update From Rep. Chamberlin
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,

In 2023, after my 1st election, **I filed a bill proposing the elimination of Property Taxes.** Then in 2024, 2025, and 2026, I filed major relief bills and my **Freedom 1,2,3 plan** to TOTALLY eliminate and replace the current property tax system.
The strategy laid out will **COMPLETELY** fund our Police, Fire, and Schools all while allowing **FLORIDA** to become the first state in the United States where you can actually own your property.
Now, after fighting for Florida citizens property tax relief, on April 1st, I released a plan that will ensure our success. _(Click the link below watch the full 10 minute press conference (and Follow me on Facebook for ongoing updates)_
---
[|
---](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=12dbd89234&e=d1c1b9864f)
| | Since the Press Conference, a series of articles and interviews are starting to pop.
Here is an article by The Florida Roundup titled:**Why Rep. Ryan Chamberlin wants to eliminate and replace Florida's property taxes**
_A Republican state representative wants to shake up Florida's entire property tax system by eliminating and replacing it._
_The effort to cut or eliminate property taxes in the state has been a top priority for Gov. Ron DeSantis, but so far, there's no official plan._
_Supporters believe cutting these taxes will help with affordability. WUSF's Douglas Soule previously reported how_[ _**critics warn**_](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=0e1de47afc&e=d1c1b9864f) _it would affect local services and require fees to be raised elsewhere._
_Lawmakers have wanted to put a measure on the November ballot to reduce property taxes. But during the session, the Florida House passed a sweeping plan that the Senate did not support._
[_**The session ended without a budget,**_](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=39b39e0e0b&e=d1c1b9864f)_so lawmakers will have to come back to hash it out. The budget has to be approved by July 1 to avoid a partial government shutdown._
_Since the likelihood that the two chambers will pass a constitutional amendment this year is on shaky ground, state Rep. Ryan Chamberlin (R-Marion County) has a backup plan._
_He wants to launch a campaign to collect enough signatures on a petition that would eliminate all property taxes on all properties in Florida. If he gets enough signatures, it could be on the ballot in 2028._
_On "The Florida Roundup," Chamberlin said he'd have a replacement plan following elimination, why he doesn't support the current system, and more._
_I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government._**Do you support doing away with all property taxes in Florida?**_Absolutely. I support doing away with the system of property taxes that also involves a replacement plan, which I have unveiled this past year. At least a first draft of one.__I do believe that we can eliminate and replace. I'm a believer that the government should not have a lien on anybody's property._**Would you include eliminating property taxes for school districts?**_I would propose eliminating — eventually — all property taxes.__Initially, homestead is where it seems like we're going to start.__But again, if I believe that the government having a lien on a personal home property is wrong, I also don't like the fact that we would have liens in school districts or liens on properties in any district.__"We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue."__I think with a $1.8 trillion economy, we can figure out a better way to generate the revenue to absolutely not cut any funding when it comes to fire departments, our safety, our schools.__We don't need to cut. We just need to figure out a different way to generate that revenue._**Eliminate the property taxes — all property taxes on all property: Residential vacation homes, commercial condominiums, school taxes, public safety taxes, all taxes, that's eventually what you'd like to get to. Is that accurate?**_Absolutely.__I think we should come to a place in this state — be the first state in the United States where people can actually own their property rather than rent it from the government.__I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place. I wouldn't have agreed with it back then either, but it's gotten out of control._**How would you propose local governments and school districts, police and fire pay for existing services and personnel?**_I think there are several ways we can do it. I have presented a few ways based on transactions. One, we would put a one-time sales fee on property.__Rather than taxing people $3,000 to $5,000 a year for the rest of their lives on one purchase, we could figure out a reasonable fee where they buy their property to put some money into the system.__I know we have 140-plus million travelers in and out of the state of Florida. They're not helping cover any of the safety fees that are on the backs of the homeowners paying for the whole state right now.__Yet, when they come here, if they're in trouble, our police take care of them, our fire takes care of them. And there's nothing that's being contributed to relieve the burden of property taxes when it comes to that.__[If] someone says, "Ryan, are you open to raising the sales tax at all?" If I have to make a choice between property tax and raising the sales tax one cent or two cents.__Every one cent in the state of Florida generates billions of dollars. We can get to the number fairly rapidly if we look at these creative transactional ways.__"I don't like the current system. I think it was designed in a time when our state was a different size, a different place."__One reason why I would lean toward a sales tax increase if we had to — I don't know that we have to.__But if we had to is because again, the 140 million people that travel to our state, then they're spending so much of that money there, it's actually relieving if we move it off the backs of the homeowners.__It would be one of the biggest tax cuts for the citizens of Florida in history. So I think we look at the numbers and figure it out._
---

* [https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/florida-lawmaker-aims-ballot-measure-ending-all-property-taxes-2028](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=4c630ea56f&e=d1c1b9864f)
* [https://www.miamitimesonline.com/business/florida-lawmaker-aims-for-ballot-measure-ending-all-property-taxes-in-2028/article_5c9a4923-af32-4e43-83a4-a046b315c221.html](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=05581fbbbd&e=d1c1b9864f)
* [https://www.wflx.com/2026/04/06/florida-lawmakers-advance-competing-proposals-cut-or-eliminate-property-taxes-ahead-special-session/](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=8471e4036f&e=d1c1b9864f)

---
|
---
| | **STAY CONNECTED FOR UPDATES:**
For continued updates and future announcements on property tax reform, I encourage you to follow along on Facebook:[https://www.facebook.com/ryanchamberlincampaign](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=d50836f735&e=d1c1b9864f)
Staying informed is important as this conversation continues, and your input will help shape what comes next.
As always, please feel free to reach out and share your thoughts.
---
| | Best regards,

Peter,

I'm the only U.S. Senate candidate in America that speaks this way. I don't take money from AIPAC or the Muslim Brotherhood. I'm probably on a CCP watchlist and the DC uniparty says I'm "unqualified", which is the best endorsement I could hope for in America. We have to rally this country, right here, right now.

We may have to start a new party with this idea in the foundations, but I'd much rather save The Republican Party. Why? I genuinely believe in the philosophy of Republicanism. The fundamental issue in America is certainly a 2 party system that is perverted and corrupted beyond recognition. Maybe beyond salvaging, but... A core component of that decay is the size of government itself and more importantly the administrative leviathan that powers it. A basic yet almost unquantifiable difference between the Republican Party and Democratic Party is Democrats have conceded to the infinite expansion of the federal government as a principle. The Republicans, at least in theory and for show, still pretend we believe in shrinking the government. Right now, I don't know how many Republicans really believe in that. We must starve and strangle this leviathan and the corruption that undergirds it.

I'm trying to help this party and our country through the mechanisms we have... if we fail to rally behind good ideas things are going to get bad. Right now the Republican Party seems much more interested in Forever Wars and Legacy Media than America. Which is obviously a losing position politically and maybe militarily. Maybe that's the whole point, throw the ball back and forth with We The People as the monkey in the middle. Gavin Newsom? Really? I continue to pray we can find a rally point of common sense, it was never going to be easy. Anybody pretending President Trump didn't open the door is being dishonest, anybody who can't bring themselves to question ANYTHING he decides has given up their citizenship. President Trump needs us to speak up and be ready to support some very tough decisions ahead, and it isn't a war in Iran, it's the constitutional crisis coming to secure elections in November. Or we will lose everything. Maybe nobody or not enough people really care anymore... That's the Greek tragedy. That's the 1984 orwellian doom! We deserve better, we can be better.

I’m asking now because that’s what moments like this require.

When a race tightens like this, the outside money, the attacks, the pressure follows – and right now, _we are feeling it._

John Braun is exactly the kind of candidate national extremists want - and now Trump’s candidate. Hardline anti-choice, backed by people who expect loyalty, not independence.

That's not who I am.

I’ve tried to lead by showing up and doing the work. You could see it this week - meeting with folks on the hatchery fight, supporting new healthcare investments on the coast. This work isn’t flashy, it’s real, and it makes a difference for Southwest Washingtonians.

**That’s what I’m fighting to keep doing.** | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129877694/615862681/2101450411?refcode=MGP_EM_FR_260421_1_1&refcode2=85ec21c4-903d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NWVjMjFjNC05MDNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pOPG2zALZxu2vR4ff7ZOXIInQwiTCaAd55QI7ZkUQwk=)

Thank you for being part of this moment.
Marie

# **Rep. Nancy Mace introduces resolution to expel Rep. Cory Mills over domestic violence, stolen valor allegations**
GOP Rep. Nancy Mace introduced a resolution Monday **[to expel Rep. Cory Mills from the House](https://substack.com/redirect/4f5bc1b5-57be-4c30-b4d0-42256870e61b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over allegations of domestic violence, sexual misconduct, stolen valor and profiteering from federal contracts while serving in Congress. Mace said "The swamp has protected Cory Mills for far too long" and accused him of "beating women and telling them to lie about it, cyberstalking women, lying about his military service, and profiting off his seat," arguing "Any Member who votes to keep him here is voting to protect a woman beater and a fraud."

# **Virginia votes on constitutional amendment that would give Dems 91% of House seats despite state being evenly split**
Virginians vote Tuesday on a constitutional amendment that would **[give Democrats 10 of 11 congressional seats (91%)](https://substack.com/redirect/fb4224d2-967b-4820-a379-6a4ed8dffb7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** despite Kamala Harris winning the state with less than 52% in 2024--creating a 39% gap between popular vote and representation. Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger, who ran as a moderate and said she had no plans to engage in redistricting, presided over what is "by some measures, the most extreme gerrymandering in the country," with ballot language asking voters if they want to "restore fairness" while the administration encouraged clerks not to display maps.
* **Democrat claims of "retaliation" don't match the data**: While Senate President Pro Tempore Louise Lucas says it's retaliation for Texas redistricting, an analysis found Texas has a 21% gap (Harris won 42%, Dems have 21% of seats) versus Virginia's proposed 39% gap. Virginia currently has one of the most fairly constituted delegations--Dems hold 55% of seats matching their vote share--while 7 of the 10 most-gerrymandered states favor Democrats.
* **How it happened** : Democrats got around Virginia's law against partisan redistricting by rescinding it and making the rescission retroactive, with Republicans saying they violated procedures by holding the first legislative vote after the early voting period began.

# **Border Czar Homan says deportation numbers will rebound, defends Minnesota operation as victory despite criticism**
Border Czar Tom Homan **[told Newsmax](https://substack.com/redirect/01cce625-4fc6-43c1-8b4d-537d26564807?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that deportation numbers, which dropped from 8,000 per week to just above 5,000, will come back up, explaining "we just hired 10,000 more agents."
## [Watch:](https://substack.com/redirect/01cce625-4fc6-43c1-8b4d-537d26564807?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **Homan claims Minnesota cooperation was the real win** : Homan rejected claims the administration surrendered, saying "We took over 4,000 people off the streets of that state, most of them criminals" and "walked away with cooperation from just about every county jail and the state prison system." He argued this cooperation makes enforcement more efficient and safer.
* **Why jail cooperation matters** : Homan explained that arresting people in jails is "safer for the officers" and "safer for the community," and frees up resources: "Rather than sending a dozen people to go look for somebody, a public safety threat in the [state] of Minnesota, now we've got one agent arresting one illegal alien in the county jail. What does that mean? That releases 11 other people to look for more people."

Nancy Mace introduced a resolution Monday over allegations of domestic violence, sexual misconduct, stolen valor and profiteering from federal contracts while serving in Congress. Mace said "The swamp has protected Cory Mills for far too long" and accused him of "beating women and telling them to lie about it, cyberstalking women, lying about his military service, and profiting off his seat," arguing "Any Member who votes to keep him here is voting to protect a woman beater and a fraud." While the committee hasn't released findings, Mace argued the evidence is "overwhelming" and "He needs to be expelled immediately." The resolution comes a week after former Reps. Tony Gonzales (R-Texas) and Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.) both resigned over sexual misconduct allegations. The House Ethics Committee has been investigating Mace since last year over allegations she improperly collected reimbursements for lodging expenses. The truth is that too few citizens know the story of America's founding. When you display this flag, you invite others to remember and learn about the founding principles of our nation.

Peter, it's Gabby Giffords.

In 2011, in the blink of an eye, my life changed forever: I was shot in the head while holding an event with constituents in a grocery store parking lot. Six people were killed that day, and 12 others were injured.

We've made real progress on gun violence prevention since then. I'll be the first to tell you, however, that there is so much more work we still must do.

Democracy, safety, and a better future for our kids are on the line in this election – and that’s why **I’m proud to endorse Jeremy Moss in the race to represent Michigan’s 11th District.**

In the legislature, Jeremy has fought to keep communities safe and delivered real results to prevent gun violence in Michigan. He recently introduced a bill to ban high-capacity magazines, which are often used in the deadliest mass shootings. He’s a leader we can count on to keep doing the hard work.

Michigan needs a champion like Jeremy who realizes the heartbreak gun violence causes in his state, and will never stop working to end it.

clean_body: Democracy, safety, and a better future for our kids are on the line in this election – and that’s why I’m proud to endorse Jeremy Moss in the race to represent Michigan’s 11th District. | = Peter, it's Gabby Giffords. Six people were killed that day, and 12 others were injured. We've made real progress on gun violence prevention since then. I'll be the first to tell you, however, that there is so much more work we still must do. Democracy, safety, and a better future for our kids are on the line in this election – and that’s why I’m proud to endorse Jeremy Moss in the race to represent Michigan’s 11th District. In the legislature, Jeremy has fought to keep communities safe and delivered real results to prevent gun violence in Michigan. He recently introduced a bill to ban high-capacity magazines, which are often used in the deadliest mass shootings. He’s a leader we can count on to keep doing the hard work. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

In recent months, a significant shift has occurred in the public conversation surrounding marijuana, as influential voices and institutions increasingly acknowledge the potential harms associated with today's high-potency cannabis products and widespread use. I'll examine three prominent social media posts that collectively signal a reevaluation of cannabis's place in American society, challenging years of progressive normalization.

Political commentator Saagar Enjeti ([@esaagar](https://substack.com/redirect/ba259881-2df9-4883-a9b6-f24d1e5a22eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) brought attention to a startling statistic that forms the cornerstone of the emerging debate: approximately 18 million Americans now smoke marijuana 21 or more days per month.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.1XjTodyJfksnLXxvssBAcW6YjFGURIPROohheZbM42A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=194912039)
This figure, derived from the National Survey on Drug Use and Health, represents a full-blown addiction crisis according to Enjeti, who accompanied his post with a reference to the New York Times editorial board's unexpected intervention on the topic.

Enjeti's post highlights how rapidly the landscape has changed since recreational marijuana legalization began spreading across states in 2012. What was once celebrated as a personal freedom issue has, for many users, become a daily dependency that rivals or exceeds tobacco in frequency of use. This daily use pattern is particularly concerning given the dramatic increase in THC concentrations in modern cannabis products compared to the marijuana of previous decades.

Perhaps most significant in this evolving conversation is the New York Times editorial board's February 2026 piece titled "**[It's Time for America to Admit That It Has a Marijuana Problem](https://substack.com/redirect/d33c4812-248c-49c2-8c42-60567e4378b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**." The board, which had previously supported legalization, now acknowledges that "the loosening of marijuana policies -- especially the decision to legalize pot without adequately regulating it -- has led to worse outcomes than many Americans expected."

This represents a remarkable institutional reversal from a publication that just over a decade earlier published a six-part series arguing for the repeal of the federal marijuana ban. The Times now admits that "not all of their arguments in support of decriminalizing marijuana have stood the test of time."

The editorial board points to several concerning trends: the rise in addiction rates, increasing instances of cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (which causes severe vomiting and abdominal pain), and more frequent emergency room visits for marijuana-linked paranoia and psychotic disorders. They also note the false perception of marijuana as a "harmless drug" with no addictive properties, pointing out that this Belief has been contradicted by mounting evidence.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f18506ab-df0a-4d8f-973a-d92d767294a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Times specifically calls out what they term "Big Weed" -- the commercial cannabis industry that has emerged in states with legalization -- for marketing practices that target vulnerable populations and for making unfounded medical claims about their products. They advocate for a policy of "grudging toleration" rather than enthusiastic endorsement, with substantial regulatory guardrails.

The third post, from user IterIntellectus ([@IterIntellectus](https://substack.com/redirect/c4de6109-1554-4e08-9a16-4be510e0651a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), takes an even more alarming perspective, stating bluntly that "weed makes you retarded" and warning of permanent cognitive effects for heavy users who began before age 18 and continued for a decade or more. While language may be crude, the concern raises legitimate neuroscientific questions about how cannabis exposure during critical periods of brain development might result in lasting changes.

This perspective reflects growing concern in medical circles about adolescent exposure to high-potency cannabis products. Research published in JAMA Network Open and other medical journals has indicated associations between early, frequent cannabis use and subsequent mental health problems in young adulthood. One study found that teens who started using cannabis early and used frequently had a 51% higher chance of seeking care for mental health problems and an 86% higher chance of needing care for physical health issues compared to non-users.

The concern about permanent cognitive effects particularly relates to adolescence, when the brain undergoes significant development and reorganization that continues into the early 20s. The endocannabinoid system, which interacts with THC, plays a crucial role in these neurological processes, and disruption during this critical developmental window may have lasting consequences.

The concerns raised in these posts must be understood in the context of how dramatically cannabis has changed from previous eras. The average THC concentration in marijuana products has risen from approximately 3-4% in the 1990s to 20-30% in many commercial products today, with concentrates reaching 80-90% THC. This pharmacological shift makes direct comparisons to historical cannabis use potentially misleading.

Compounding this change in potency is the variety of consumption methods now available. Vaping, dabbing, and edibles create different patterns of exposure and intoxication compared to traditional smoking. These products often allow for more discreet use and higher dosing, contributing to the patterns of daily consumption highlighted in Enjeti's tweet.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/69be2a5f-be5f-4d9c-adcd-65aa3007e032?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Traffic accident statistics went up after Colorado turned their entire government into a Pot Dispensary. (A 151% spike in impaired driving accidents and a 300% spike in fatalities from same) By then, they were making so much money, CO chose to bury the stats. [Over 40% of fatal crash victims](https://substack.com/redirect/13f99edb-a7a0-466a-9324-86a78b7ac588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had THC levels far above legal limits, showing cannabis use before driving remains widespread. The rate didn't drop after legalization, suggesting policy changes haven't altered risky habits. Experts warn that the lack of public awareness around marijuana's dangers behind the wheel is putting lives at risk.
The collective alarm points to a need for nuanced policy approaches that acknowledge both the failures of prohibition and the limitations of the current commercial legalization paradigm. The Times editorial board suggests several regulatory measures including:

\- Limiting THC concentrations in commercially available products
\- Restricting marketing practices that appeal to adolescents
\- Clear warnings about potential risks, particularly for pregnant women and those with pre-existing mental health conditions
\- Crackdowns on unsubstantiated medical claims made by dispensaries
\- Potentially creating consumption venue restrictions to reduce public use
These suggestions emerge from a recognition that the current "hands-off" approach to regulation in many states has created an environment resembling that of tobacco before public health interventions addressed its harms.

The three posts examined here represent different facets of a growing consensus that America's relationship with cannabis needs reassessment. From the statistical warnings about daily use patterns to institutional acknowledgment of policy failures and concerns about neurological impacts, a more cautious approach is emerging.

This doesn't necessarily imply a return to the criminalization models of the past, but rather a more sophisticated regulatory framework that acknowledges both the potential benefits and harms of cannabis use. As the Times editorial board concluded, "It is time to acknowledge reality and change course" -- a sentiment that reflects how quickly the conversation around marijuana has evolved from enthusiastic endorsement to concerned reckoning.

The challenge now lies in developing evidence-based policies that reduce harms while recognizing that cannabis, like alcohol and tobacco, will remain part of American society regardless of its legal status. The posts examined here represent important milestones in shifting the conversation from simple legalization questions to more complex considerations of how to integrate cannabis into society responsibly.

name: Amanda for Colorado
subject: This is what running elections actually looks
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Amanda for Colorado
body:
| | | Hi Peter **Election Day is usually about a 21-hour work day for me.** Vote centers open at 7 a.m. and my phone is ringing from the moment I wake up. Media heard a rumor (it’s false, again) and want an official explanation. Medical emergency at a vote center. Someone is using their vehicle to block access to a drop box. Weather changes the plan. That’s just the first few hours, and those are the easy problems. I’ll be at elections HQ until 4 a.m. the next morning, making sure every verified ballot is counted. In Jefferson County, my team and I prepare for problems, solve them fast and strategically, and make sure **nothing gets between a voter and their vote.** These days, that means not just having a plan for when the power goes out, but having a plan for when the mail stops or a ballot box is attacked or a federal agency shows up with a big truck and big demands. That’s what running elections actually looks like now. **What should make every voter angry is that your election officials have to make plans to thwart Trump’s attempts to sow chaos in your elections.** That people in power are trying to make voting harder on purpose.
