body:
Congress can reverse the bad USPS policies being forced onto our postal workers by MAGA "reformers" searching for DOGE-like "efficiency". We just need to remind Congress to do their jobs and protect this vital public service.
Write your letter and help save the Post Office by demanding Congress stop efforts to privatize the USPS now >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks: The United States Postal Service is being pushed toward a financial breaking point that could cause it to run out of cash as soon as February of next year, and only Congress can fix it.
The Postmaster General has warned that the current financial crisis at USPS could “ lead to the end of the Postal Service as we know it” if lawmakers fail to act. This crisis did not come out of nowhere. It is the result of years of bad postal policy decisions that drained billions from the Postal Service and tied its hands.
Donald Trump and his greedy corporate buddies would love to see a privatized Postal Service. They want to throw entire communities under the bus, outsource delivery, and sell the post office off piecemeal to make millions. We cannot allow that to happen. It would mean higher costs for families, the risk of service shutdowns for rural communities, and the loss of a public institution that guarantees universal access to mail.
Send your letter now: Congress must remove the financial barriers that will allow USPS to stabilize its finances and create a sustainable future >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
In 2022, the Postal Service Reform Act was one step that ended requirements such as the pre-funding of retiree health benefits and restrictions on pricing and some service expansion.
It is time to completely untie the Postal Service’s hands and allow the agency to fully manage benefit and retirement funds, pension investments, and to extend the agency’s borrowing authority that hasn’t been adjusted for inflation since 1992. Congress must reverse the law restricting the USPS from providing new services that could generate new streams of revenue.
The Postal Service is not supposed to be a profit machine. It is a lifeline for communities across the country. Removing these policy restrictions will allow the Postal Service to continue delivering our mail and serving the public effectively, saving the agency billions of dollars per year.
Take action to save the Post Office! Demand Congress reverse bad postal policy and stop privatization now >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-the-privatization-of-the-usps/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

Peter,

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is coming to Congress to defend his latest budget priorities, and what he's pushing would be disastrous for our public health system.

As Secretary of Health and Human Services, he's advanced a 2026 budget built around his "Make America Healthy Again" agenda and a sweeping restructuring of the department altogether.

But the branding isn't the point— _the cuts are._

His proposals would slash major public health agencies like the CDC and NIH. It would shift resources away from infectious disease response and the core systems communities rely on to prepare for and respond to outbreaks.

This isn't a minor adjustment. It points to a very different direction for public health in this country, **and Kim isn't going to let it slide.**

As a doctor, she's spent her career taking care of patients, even when systems were stretched thin. She knows exactly what these kinds of cuts look like in real life—slower responses to outbreaks, fewer tools to track diseases, and less support for the research that drives new treatments and breakthroughs.

**She's preparing to question RFK Jr. directly and force a real conversation about what his budget would mean for patients and families.** Because when these systems are weakened, people feel it immediately.

clean_body: Peter, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is coming to Congress to defend his latest budget priorities, and what he's pushing would be disastrous for our public health system. As Secretary of Health and Human Services, he's advanced a 2026 budget built around his "Make America Healthy Again" agenda and a sweeping restructuring of the department altogether. But the branding isn't the point— the cuts are. His proposals would slash major public health agencies like the CDC and NIH. It would shift resources away from infectious disease response and the core systems communities rely on to prepare for and respond to outbreaks. This isn't a minor adjustment. It points to a very different direction for public health in this country, and Kim isn't going to let it slide. As a doctor, she's spent her career taking care of patients, even when systems were stretched thin. She knows exactly what these kinds of cuts look like in real life—slower responses to outbreaks, fewer tools to track diseases, and less support for the research that drives new treatments and breakthroughs. She's preparing to question RFK Jr. directly and force a real conversation about what his budget would mean for patients and families. name: Jen Kiggans
subject: I’ll be honest with you, Peter.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
I never planned on being a politician.

| I'll be honest with you, Peter.
I never planned on being a politician.
I was just a mom of four who was fed up with the way the Democrats and career politicians were running our country into the ground. So, I decided to get off the sidelines and actually do something about it.
But right now, I am in the middle of one of the tightest, must-win congressional races in the entire country, and the Democrats are coming after me with absolutely EVERYTHING they've got.
---
| [SUPPORT JEN KIGGANS FOR CONGRESS >>](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
---
You see, service runs deep in my family. My Grandfather was a Navy postalman in WWII, my Dad was a Green Beret in Vietnam, and my husband is a retired Navy F/A-18 pilot who flew in the Middle East. Now, one of our sons is carrying that exact same torch serving in the Navy.
I spent my own time in the military as a Navy helicopter pilot flying H-46s and H-3s in the Persian Gulf. My call sign was "Blossom" - a joke that stuck after another female pilot and I cut out reflective tape in the shape of bathtub non-skid flower stickers and slapped them on our flight helmets.
After serving in the Navy, I used my GI Bill benefits to become an Adult-Geriatric Primary Care Nurse Practitioner. Caring for our "Greatest Generation" has been the honor of my lifetime, and it really cemented my service-first attitude.
It is that EXACT same attitude I took to Washington. As a mother of two sons and two daughters, I am DETERMINED to make sure the country we leave to our children is better than the one we inherited.
---
| [SUPPORT JEN KIGGANS FOR CONGRESS >>](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
---
But the radical Left has not forgotten that we flipped this district RED in 2022, and they are furious.
They're so desperate to defeat me that they are actually trying to REDRAW the Virginia election maps just to take me out. On top of that, my opponent is being propped up by far-Left, national Democrats, and just announced a staggering $1.75 MILLION RAISED this past quarter alone.
I've been attacked by the radical left, lied about on TV ads, and even had my campaign office vandalized!
But I'm not afraid. I'm a fighter, and I'm not going to let them intimidate me.
I've never backed down from a tough mission, but I cannot fight off the Democrat machine and their MILLIONS alone. If we are going to hold this seat and protect our conservative majority, I need your help right now.
[So, if you're willing to support this former Navy helicopter pilot and nurse practitioner on this mission to SAVE our GOP majority, I am asking - humbly \- if you'll consider chipping in just a few bucks today.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
Every little bit counts, and I promise to use every penny to fight against the radical Left and their millions of dollars.
You've read this far, so I know you care. [Can you give me a chance to keep fighting for our community?](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._Na1myPGTw)
---
| [SUPPORT JEN KIGGANS FOR CONGRESS >>](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-q2tiiCwAFP2eqA)
---
I truly couldn't do any of this without your kindness and generosity. Thank you..!
Sincerely,
Jen Kiggans

I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger.

body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,

To win the future we deserve, we all need to step up now like never before. | | | Peter — Working people are being robbed. In the richest country in the world, the cost of everything is going up while paychecks stay the same or go down. And the same crooks overcharging us and underpaying us now say they want to replace us with robots. But the people? They see it. They see how the government can find the money for everything _but_ working families. How we find money for Trump’s tax breaks for the wealthy. How we find billions for wars and coups. **The truth is that we DO have the resources to make sure every person who calls this country home has the things they need to build a good life.** To support their families. To leave something for our kids and grandkids. In the wealthiest country in the history of the world, none of this should be considered a radical idea. But to win the future we deserve, we all need to step up now like never before. [**That’s why I’m so proud to officially announce the launch of our national Working Families Guarantee, the cornerstone of our economic agenda for working people. is what we’re going to demand of the wealthy and well-connected, and the politicians in their pocket. It means you will have a home you can afford. It means that AI call centers won’t be driving up your energy costs. It means you can go to the doctor without worrying about how you’ll pay for it. It means you’ll have low-cost childcare, and that everyone will have 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave. It means you’ll have a good job that pays the bills AND allows you to enjoy your life. None of this is pie in the sky. We know, because the Working Families Party has won these kinds of victories for working families in state after state for more than two decades. We have worked to pass first-of-their-kind paid family leave and sick time programs in states like Connecticut and New Jersey. We’ve guaranteed child care in New Mexico, and we’re about to do it in New York City. **The path is clear. clean_body: To win the future we deserve, we all need to step up now like never before. | | | Peter — Working people are being robbed. In the richest country in the world, the cost of everything is going up while paychecks stay the same or go down. And the same crooks overcharging us and underpaying us now say they want to replace us with robots. But the people? They see it. They see how the government can find the money for everything but working families. How we find money for Trump’s tax breaks for the wealthy. How we find billions for wars and coups. The truth is that we DO have the resources to make sure every person who calls this country home has the things they need to build a good life. To support their families. To leave something for our kids and grandkids. In the wealthiest country in the history of the world, none of this should be considered a radical idea. But to win the future we deserve, we all need to step up now like never before. The national is what we’re going to demand of the wealthy and well-connected, and the politicians in their pocket. It means you will have a home you can afford. It means that AI call centers won’t be driving up your energy costs. It means you can go to the doctor without worrying about how you’ll pay for it. It means you’ll have low-cost childcare, and that everyone will have 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave. It means you’ll have a good job that pays the bills AND allows you to enjoy your life. None of this is pie in the sky. We know, because the Working Families Party has won these kinds of victories for working families in state after state for more than two decades. We have worked to pass first-of-their-kind paid family leave and sick time programs in states like Connecticut and New Jersey. We’ve guaranteed child care in New Mexico, and we’re about to do it in New York City. The path is clear. We are going to take on the wealthy and well-connected who have rigged our economy and our politics against working people, and who have hoarded all the wealth for themselves. We know this won’t happen in one year, or just one election. But this is a fight we will win — if we all stand together to demand what we deserve. And we’ll follow up with ways that you can get involved in this fight. In solidarity, Maurice Mitchell National Director Working Families Party Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. # [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41190%2E3422442%2EFWKW_4)
Peter,
It’s been another week on the Whiteboard Warriors Tour, and I wanted to share a quick update.
I’m running to represent every pocket of California, and that means getting out there and showing up—no matter what.
Some days that looks like hours in the car between towns, packed schedules, and yes... realizing there’s nowhere to stop for lunch along the way and making do with a very squashed protein bar.
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260421_1_ak.6oSKED&refcode=em20260421-41190&%3Bamounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41190%2E3422442%2EFWKW_4)
**But that’s the job.**
Every stop means hearing directly from Californians about what’s actually happening in their lives—not what lobbyists say, not what consultants poll, but what families are dealing with every day.
And here’s what I’m hearing:
Costs are out of control. Housing. Child care. Groceries. People are doing everything right and still falling behind.
**I’m running to change that, and I’m doing it the same way I always have: no corporate PAC money, no special interest checks. Just people.**
But that means this campaign runs on grassroots supporters chipping in what they can, when they can.
**[If you’re able, will you pitch in $5 to help keep me on the road, reach more voters, and keep this tour going?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260421_1_ak.6oSKED&refcode=em20260421-41190&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=4&akid=41190%2E3422442%2EFWKW_4)**

Thank you,
Katie

| | Republicans aren't backing down from passing the SAVE Act, and we must not back down from blocking it! They're already looking for new ways to pass it — including using budget reconciliation to jam it through with a simple majority vote. Let's be clear about what this bill really does. Trump and Republicans claim it's about stopping NON-CITIZENS from voting. That's simply not true. It's about making it hard for millions of CITIZENS to vote — the citizens the Republicans want to stop from voting in order to rig the November election! Hard for women who've changed their last names. Hard for students and Tribal members who couldn't use their standard IDs to vote. Hard for city dwellers who would have to vote at polling places where the Republicans could slow down voting to create long lines and cause citizens to give up. Hard for working people who don't have easy access to documents like passports or birth certificates. And if you're purged from the voter rolls by the Trump administration? You might not get re-registered in time. The process is complicated, expensive, and in many cases, unrealistic. This bill is blatant voter suppression, and it's part of Trump's broader MAGA strategy we've seen before: change the rules, create confusion, and make it harder for certain Americans to participate in our democracy. I've been fighting the SAVE Act in the Senate, and I'm preparing for the next phase of this battle if Republicans try to pass this bill through reconciliation. The right to vote is fundamental. It is the beating heart of our democracy. And I will not stand by while Trump and Republicans try to rig the system to hold onto power. name: Tom Leonard
subject: April 21st - Positive Path Newsletter
body:
[](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/LrF1oEtsK1Q1Mr2j3x3XFg/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA)
---
Dear Friend,

I hope you are doing well!

April is almost done, and we had some exciting updates from the campaign trail this week.
* We officially submitted and filed all our petitions to be on the ballot for Governor, and I say 'we' because my whole family was there with me to enjoy the moment, and I am so grateful.
* I had the great opportunity to tour Common Ground and see firsthand the important work they're doing to support those facing mental health challenges. A special thank you to Janet Sarkos for the tour.
* I had the opportunity to speak to the Republican Women's Club of Monroe County.
* I attended a data center meeting in Gaines Charter Township and listened to and spoke with many local community members, continuing to spread our vision for dealing with rising energy costs and monopoly utilities.
* I was the keynote speaker for the Shiawassee County GOP's annual breakfast

---
**Looking Ahead to This Week**
This week will be packed with many events around the state, focusing on reaching local communities, everyday Michiganders, and hearing more about what we need to do to help fix our state when I'm its next Governor.
* For starters, we're releasing the 4th edition of our policy plan, The PathForward this week, which you can check out at tomformichigan.com
* I am hosting another town hall, this one focused on energy costs, and the monopoly utilities. It's an unscripted, completely open event to hear my plan, and share more ideas out there.
* I will be at the Eastside Republican Club Gubernatorial Forum this week, and I couldn't be more excited to have another opportunity to answer questions and share my plan for Michigan.
* I will be hosting another roundtable, this one taking place in Midland.

---
This week will be another busy one, but I am so excited for another week of going around Michigan, speaking with local community leaders, and sharing our campaigns positive vision.
**Join the Team!**
It's with your help that results come. We would love to have you join the team!

• Volunteer Today: Sign up for phone banking, door-knocking, events, or hosting a meet-and-greet in your community. Your time makes all the difference! [Sign Up Here](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/UgaGPRhsdPa4zFm7638Ol1vw/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA) and reach out to our Field Director, Tony, for more volunteer opportunities at [tony@tomformichigan.com](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/oMFQv4UDRugMHmey763m8I8w/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA)

• Continue sharing our positive vision on social media - follow my X account's, [@Tom4Michigan](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/8mfxmPxfgiId5rUIruzrPQ/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA) and [@TomLeonard28](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/D8Mv7PX24A0fQLEbt81zvg/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA), my [Facebook page](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/4d0mHwopmEklBdfrsviUVQ/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA), my [Instagram](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/3mAeo6dXB1u9mVEnBcizKw/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA), and my [TikTok](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/fIZc763Gu3wM8Xpi4fyBWi9Q/0hEtSbr4OIkLlNIIM3GhYA).
---
Thank you for your continued support of our vision, and helping us share our Path Forward for Michigan across the state. Let's keep our momentum going into this upcoming week, and through the end of April!
---

God bless you and your loved ones. Have a great week.

Best,

**Tom Leonard**
Candidate for Governor

clean_body: Dear Friend, I hope you are doing well! April is almost done, and we had some exciting updates from the campaign trail this week. We officially submitted and filed all our petitions to be on the ballot for Governor, and I say 'we' because my whole family was there with me to enjoy the moment, and I am so grateful. I had the great opportunity to tour Common Ground and see firsthand the important work they're doing to support those facing mental health challenges. A special thank you to Janet Sarkos for the tour. I had the opportunity to speak to the Republican Women's Club of Monroe County. I attended a data center meeting in Gaines Charter Township and listened to and spoke with many local community members, continuing to spread our vision for dealing with rising energy costs and monopoly utilities. I was the keynote speaker for the Shiawassee County GOP's annual breakfast Looking Ahead to This Week This week will be packed with many events around the state, focusing on reaching local communities, everyday Michiganders, and hearing more about what we need to do to help fix our state when I'm its next Governor. For starters, we're releasing the 4th edition of our policy plan, The PathForward this week, which you can check out at tomformichigan.com I am hosting another town hall, this one focused on energy costs, and the monopoly utilities. It's an unscripted, completely open event to hear my plan, and share more ideas out there. I will be at the Eastside Republican Club Gubernatorial Forum this week, and I couldn't be more excited to have another opportunity to answer questions and share my plan for Michigan. I will be hosting another roundtable, this one taking place in Midland. This week will be another busy one, but I am so excited for another week of going around Michigan, speaking with local community leaders, and sharing our campaigns positive vision. Join the Team! name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
subject: Some news
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Some news: Thanks to your grassroots support, Alexandria has raised more money than any other member in the House of Representatives this cycle!
We wanted to take this opportunity to thank you so much for being a part of this movement for a better world. This is no small feat, given that our average donation floats around just $16. But with your help, we’re able to organize across NY-14 and the country:
**This past Sunday, we officially launched our 2026 organizing operation** to re-elect Alexandria this year — starting by winning the primary election on June 23rd.
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260421.Uue4Nk&refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260421.Uue4Nk&refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260421.Uue4Nk&refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)
**Our community outreach efforts are only possible because of your support.** And when community comes together, real change becomes possible.
Alexandria doesn’t do a minute of call time or take a dime from corporate PACs. When thousands of us donate $5 at a time, it all adds up to create a powerful movement.
Now, Alexandria is facing two opponents in the Democratic primary election on June 23rd. One of them is a former Wall Street banker who doesn’t even live in NY-14.
[ If you can, please donate $5 right now to support our organizers and volunteers across NY-14 and ensure they have the resources to reach voters across our district.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260421.Uue4Nk&refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260421.Uue4Nk&refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)**
Whether or not you can afford to donate today, thank you for being a part of this campaign. We’re so grateful that you’re here.
Pa’lante,
Team AOC

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/aoc-email-20260421?refcode=em20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=24&refcode2=11226_2526796_MdQqwD&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)** | **[Merch](https://shop.ocasiocortez.com/?utm_source=em-footer-20260421-11226-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=25&akid=11226%2E2526796%2EMdQqwD)**

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end. Small donors like you keep us going. To contribute via check, please address to Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, PO Box 680080, Corona, NY 11368.

## The media under Trump 2.0
This Saturday, the WHCA will be holding the White House Correspondents' Dinner.
It's a swanky event at the Washington Hilton Hotel, where the who's who in lefty media congratulate each other on their great, hard-hitting journalism (yes that's sarcasm).
As the event approaches, I've been thinking about the state of the American media: more specifically, how far it's fallen.
In fact, the only reason why the event is relevant this year is because President Trump will be in attendance--for the first time in his two terms.
It's a huge break for the WHCA (honestly, I wish the President did not go).
Without his presence it would be crystal clear just how irrelevant they've become.
Yet members of the WHCA are publicly trashing President Trump for attending:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8751df17-5967-4621-900f-827c6e2d1899?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I talk about why traditional media has become irrelevant in Trump 2.0:
"Many cheered for the total censorship of a former president who tens of millions of Americans voted into office.
These so-called journalists who collect their income--often a lucrative one--from peddling sensationalized disinformation to the American public, especially as it has related to the Russia Hoax."
[Order Trump 2.0 HERE!](https://substack.com/redirect/2090327f-b598-4a5f-99e6-dc15ddc18862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When you consistently lie and play sides, there are consequences.
And that's exactly what the media is finding out.

---
Peter,
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg's for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and started working for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life's easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself - but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.
Working at Kellogg's used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that lets you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire someday.
But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost-of-living adjustments weren't keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn't right. They were making record profits - and doing it off the backs of workers.
So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RuWya2YfeKbs0RjAuBoW8kUGpoYQ8U_VKWOYAi_1iFwXCcTTZ_6QZBHdSCYprvxcPvyWLGGH6Qkp-euLYtGWimnlCufETBip-y6OLm05lWhMBRN8UemF7GFzyiFuw7oEOGKmsijZ27ZvItDE8EnHXgLMKViPbVvMI4ggBMujFgJ6WH76odgbBc_100FpUrFLZbHwqRqUlT2Ccm0tl9wu7tzbvKtroyh5ESnpB94HdVs=&c=mRYUgrM3StBHeDo32SY10-fQRWxcTrx-yIa90-t_qyEKLdE3Xz5diw==&ch=-jG736mYTP3sHTJ5pl4FyYvhyCOMBVBzVc_t3oIuYK5jtdpu-oakLQ==)
---
Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RuWya2YfeKbs0RjAuBoW8kUGpoYQ8U_VKWOYAi_1iFwXCcTTZ_6QZBHdSCYprvxcPvyWLGGH6Qkp-euLYtGWimnlCufETBip-y6OLm05lWhMBRN8UemF7GFzyiFuw7oEOGKmsijZ27ZvItDE8EnHXgLMKViPbVvMI4ggBMujFgJ6WH76odgbBc_100FpUrFLZbHwqRqUlT2Ccm0tl9wu7r6Fj06bT21AiimjEHjNwic=&c=mRYUgrM3StBHeDo32SY10-fQRWxcTrx-yIa90-t_qyEKLdE3Xz5diw==&ch=-jG736mYTP3sHTJ5pl4FyYvhyCOMBVBzVc_t3oIuYK5jtdpu-oakLQ==)
---

It's easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions - and just accept that that's how things will always be. But that's not me.
Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians - U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer - and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.
Now, I'm running again for the U.S. Senate - this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts - and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%.
I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska's Senate seat for working-class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we're going to win.

Those were the last words Amber Nicole Thurman said to her own mother before being taken into surgery.
She should have lived.
Doctors say a routine procedure could have saved her--but they waited, fearing prosecution under Georgia's abortion ban. That delay cost Amber her life and left her son without a mother. This is not an isolated tragedy. It is the direct consequence of decisions made by the Georgia Supreme Court.

| Make no mistake, the stakes in Georgia's Supreme Court election are life and death. On May 19, Georgia voters will decide whether to keep justices who helped reinstate this devastating law--or begin to change the direction of the court.
Incumbent Justices Charlie Bethel and Sarah Warren were part of the majority that allowed this ban to take effect.
Last week, both justices were endorsed by Frontline Policy Action, a powerful anti-abortion group working to push even more extreme policies. The Southern Poverty Law Center describes FPA as "ultra conservative" and says its goals "largely involve changing public policy in Georgia to align with far-right anti-abortion and anti-LGBTQ ideologies."
At the same time, their pro-rights, pro-democracy challengers, Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin, announced their endorsements by Planned Parenthood Votes and Reproductive Freedom For All.
This is the choice. And it could not be more stark.
Life or death. Freedom or control. Rights protected--or taken away. Defend Our Courts has already proven what's possible with back-to-back wins in the Pennsylvania and Wisconsin Supreme Court races.
Georgia is next, and it lays the foundation to flip Georgia's Supreme Court, but only if we act immediately. We are working to support a full-scale effort to reach voters across Georgia, but there is a critical funding gap that must be closed right now to keep this program fully operational.
If we don't step in, this opportunity could slip away.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor

This weekend was the Michigan Democratic Convention. I left the convention
feeling grateful, energized, and ready for what’s ahead.

The energy in the room was incredible. People from every corner of our
state showed up ready to organize, to build, and to win this November.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4079?t=1001&akid=1598%2E181023%2E6yGZxF ]Jocelyn Benson and supporters at the Michigan Democratic Convention.

I had the chance to talk with so many Michiganders — volunteers,
organizers, and folks who are stepping up for the first time. There’s a
real belief that we can move this state forward, and a shared commitment
to doing the work to make it happen.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4079?t=1002&akid=1598%2E181023%2E6yGZxF ]Jocelyn Benson with members of SEIU.[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4079?t=1003&akid=1598%2E181023%2E6yGZxF ] [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4079?t=1004&akid=1598%2E181023%2E6yGZxF ]Jocelyn Benson with a
supporter during the Michigan Democratic Convention.

Of course, we know this race won’t be easy. National Republicans have made
Michigan a top target, and outside groups are already pouring money in.

But what I saw at the convention reminded me why I’m so confident in what
we’re building together. This campaign is powered by people who care
deeply about the future of this state and are willing to put in the work
to protect it.

That kind of energy and commitment matters, but now our job is to keep
building on that momentum — to reach more people, grow this movement, and
make sure we’re ready for everything that’s coming next.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/4079?t=1005&akid=1598%2E181023%2E6yGZxF ]So, if you’re just fired up as I am to keep Michigan blue this November
and elect Democrats up and down the ballot, I hope you’ll chip in to my
campaign today to show the GOP we’re ready for a bright blue wave!

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your

Every time I planned to write this email, something jumped up and pushed it back.
Which means you've probably already heard that we won our case against Ticketmaster / Live Nation. The jury found them to be an unlawful monopoly.
I wanted to break the news to you, but instead I'll give you the inside story on how the case went down. It's a good one.
Quick recap:
I was part of a big group of AGs bringing this case, but the lead partner was USDOJ. We worked together for about two years to get ready for trial. This was going to be one of the biggest antitrust cases in years, which meant all hands on deck. A massive effort.
Eight weeks ago, the jury trial began.
The first week went great. Good witnesses, good evidence, and a clear picture for the jury of how Live Nation and Ticketmaster were using their monopoly to rip people off.
Then USDOJ dropped a bomb.
They had cut a secret deal with Live Nation, and they were bailing on the case.
The deal was terrible. It was an obvious sweetheart deal that even USDOJ's lead attorney in the courtroom wasn't aware of until it was announced - which means the deal didn't happen in the courthouse, it happened in Washington. It was basically a huge favor to Ticketmaster / Live Nation.
Then USDOJ tried to pressure the AGs to join their deal. They gave us 24 hours.
The vast majority of us said, "No thanks, we're going to finish the trial."
Which was the right decision, but risky. It meant we had to scramble to fill the hole in our case left by USDOJ, which had been handling most of the witnesses.
So we pooled our resources, reshuffled the workload, and hit the gas.
For the next six weeks, we marched the jury through a huge amount of evidence showing that this monopoly had crushed the competition, then used your lack of choices to raise prices on you and treat performers unfairly.
By the closing argument, we felt pretty good, but you never know what a jury will do.
The jury deliberated for four very long days, then rendered their verdict:
Unanimous on all counts, for us.
_A knockout win._
Now comes the remedy stage. The judge decides, but we get to make arguments, and we will. We believe the company should be broken up and pay a serious fine for overcharging you for years. More on that soon.
For now, I just want to offer real gratitude to the Republican and Democratic AGs who stuck with this case and finished it. That decision is going to matter to consumers and performers for a long time.
### **Called before the House Oversight Committee**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5ae95df-16ee-48a2-8e5d-3bbf7715a306?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
About a month ago, a member of my staff poked her head into my office.
"You've been summoned before the House Oversight Committee."
This wasn't a big surprise. It's a wide-ranging committee that's been highly active and it made sense they'd call me in at some point.
They're not shy about having a partisan agenda, but they also serve a legitimate oversight function, and it's my responsibility to answer their questions honestly.
They told us the topic was Medicaid fraud, so they called me and the Department of Health and Human Services Secretary to testify.
Two different jurisdictions are in play here. Our office goes after Medicaid provider fraud. NCDHHS goes after recipient fraud.
And when it comes to provider fraud, the numbers are clear: our team is one of the best in the country. We bring big cases at a steady clip. Just last month our office convicted five fraudsters who were then ordered to repay $12.7 million after billing for scores of medical services that never happened.
They quizzed us for about three hours, threw plenty of fastballs, but for the most part they played fair and it went well.
One bonus from the day:
Owen told me a week earlier that he was learning about checks and balances at school, so I told him about my upcoming testimony - and he asked if he could come. I said sure, and he sat in the second row and watched me testify. It made for a great conversation on the drive home.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f9ce1ada-b40d-4c14-8408-40b021b0fb18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
More to tell you, but this is getting long. Wishing you all the best, and I'll update you on a few other things next week.
Best,
Jeff

clean_body: And I get called before House Oversight | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more And I get called before House Oversight | | | Apr 21 | | | | | | | | | | | | Every time I planned to write this email, something jumped up and pushed it back. Which means you've probably already heard that we won our case against Ticketmaster / Live Nation. The jury found them to be an unlawful monopoly. I wanted to break the news to you, but instead I'll give you the inside story on how the case went down. It's a good one. Quick recap: I was part of a big group of AGs bringing this case, but the lead partner was USDOJ. We worked together for about two years to get ready for trial. This was going to be one of the biggest antitrust cases in years, which meant all hands on deck. A massive effort. Eight weeks ago, the jury trial began. The first week went great. Good witnesses, good evidence, and a clear picture for the jury of how Live Nation and Ticketmaster were using their monopoly to rip people off. Then USDOJ dropped a bomb. They had cut a secret deal with Live Nation, and they were bailing on the case. The deal was terrible. It was an obvious sweetheart deal that even USDOJ's lead attorney in the courtroom wasn't aware of until it was announced - which means the deal didn't happen in the courthouse, it happened in Washington. It was basically a huge favor to Ticketmaster / Live Nation. Then USDOJ tried to pressure the AGs to join their deal. They gave us 24 hours. The vast majority of us said, "No thanks, we're going to finish the trial." Which was the right decision, but risky. It meant we had to scramble to fill the hole in our case left by USDOJ, which had been handling most of the witnesses. So we pooled our resources, reshuffled the workload, and hit the gas. For the next six weeks, we marched the jury through a huge amount of evidence showing that this monopoly had crushed the competition, then used your lack of choices to raise prices on you and treat performers unfairly. By the closing argument, we felt pretty good, but you never know what a jury will do. The jury deliberated for four very long days, then rendered their verdict: Unanimous on all counts, for us. A knockout win. Now comes the remedy stage. The judge decides, but we get to make arguments, and we will. We believe the company should be broken up and pay a serious fine for overcharging you for years. More on that soon. For now, I just want to offer real gratitude to the Republican and Democratic AGs who stuck with this case and finished it. That decision is going to matter to consumers and performers for a long time. Called before the House Oversight Committee | | ---|---|--- About a month ago, a member of my staff poked her head into my office. "You've been summoned before the House Oversight Committee." This wasn't a big surprise. It's a wide-ranging committee that's been highly active and it made sense they'd call me in at some point. They're not shy about having a partisan agenda, but they also serve a legitimate oversight function, and it's my responsibility to answer their questions honestly. They told us the topic was Medicaid fraud, so they called me and the Department of Health and Human Services Secretary to testify. Two different jurisdictions are in play here. Our office goes after Medicaid provider fraud. NCDHHS goes after recipient fraud. And when it comes to provider fraud, the numbers are clear: our team is one of the best in the country. We bring big cases at a steady clip. Just last month our office convicted five fraudsters who were then ordered to repay $12.7 million after billing for scores of medical services that never happened. They quizzed us for about three hours, threw plenty of fastballs, but for the most part they played fair and it went well. One bonus from the day: Owen told me a week earlier that he was learning about checks and balances at school, so I told him about my upcoming testimony - and he asked if he could come. I said sure, and he sat in the second row and watched me testify. It made for a great conversation on the drive home. | | ---|---|--- More to tell you, but this is getting long. Wishing you all the best, and I'll update you on a few other things next week. Best, Jeff ? | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Jeff Jackson Jeff Jackson for Attorney General, P.O. *

As voters begin casting ballots, every dollar we raise now goes directly toward reaching them on TV, digital, and on the ground across Georgia.

Onward.

| | | Team,Thank you for helping get Andy Beck on the ballot for Congress.
We need nomination signatures from registered voters living in Wisconsin’s 5th Congressional District. Signatures must be dated on or after April 15, 2026, and each signer must include their full residential address (no P.O. Boxes), municipality, printed name, and date. Our goal is to submit signatures in Madison by May 27, ahead of the June 1 deadline.
Best places to gather signatures:
• Farmers markets
• Street festivals
• Public parks
• Protests and rallies
• Outside grocery stores (with permission)
• Community meetings and local events
Great opportunities in the district include:
• West Bend Farmers' Market – Saturdays, 7:30–11:00 AM, Downtown; 2026 season starts May 16• Waukesha Farmers' Market – Saturdays, 8:00 AM–12:00 PM, Downtown starts May 16
• Whitewater City Market – Tuesdays, 4:00–7:00 PM, May–October• Beaver Dam Farmers Market – Saturdays, 8:00 AM–12:00 PM, Starts May 2
**Memorial Day Weekend – Major Signature Push** Monday, May 25 is one of our best signature gathering opportunities before we head to Madison to submit petitions.
Strong Memorial Day activities include:• West Bend Memorial Day Parade — 9:30 AM Downtown West Bend• Brookfield, Waukesha, Menomonee Falls & New Berlin Memorial Day parades and ceremonies• Jefferson, Fort Atkinson, Watertown & Lake Mills Memorial Day parades and cemetery ceremonies• Beaver Dam, Hartford, Mayville & Horicon Memorial Day parades and veterans’ events
These events bring large family crowds, veteran’s groups, and strong community turnout—excellent places to gather signatures.
Two other events in Waukesha County are:• **End the War Now** protest in Brookfield from Saturday April 25th, 10:30 AM-Noon on Bluemound between Main St. and Executive Drive Brookfield• **Workers Over Billionaires** protest in Waukesha at Cutler Park Friday May 1st,11:00 am-12:30 PM. 321 Wisconsin Ave Waukesha
Remember: signing a nomination paper does NOT mean someone is voting for Andy—it simply helps ensure voters have a choice on the ballot.
Nomination petitions and instructions can be downloaded from the Beck for Congress website. Please reply with where you can help gather signatures.
Thank you for stepping up.Andy
**“A change will do you good”**

## “House District 2 candidate waves flag for peace in bid for seat in Congress”

**The headline nails it. This campaign is all about leading with peace. It’s the reason I decided to run in the first place.**
**In fact, I remember the exact moment I decided to run:** In 2024, Jared Huffman voted in favor of sending more than **$26 billion** in supplemental aid to Israel, despite clear evidence of ethnic cleansing and genocide. I did the math. That amounted to over **$60 million dollars per Congressional District.**
**Couldn’t families in our communities have used that money? When I saw that vote, I decided that the twelve-year incumbent had to be challenged.**
Today, things have spiraled even farther out of control. Israel and the U.S. are now engaged in a war with Iran that is likely to resume in the coming days as the tentative ceasefire expires. The cost for that war has already surpassed **$57 billion** — combined with the supplemental aid, that’s **$190 million dollars per Congressional District**!
I believe that every dollar that goes to human rights abusers and war is a dollar that is stolen from our healthcare, child care, education, housing, energy grid, and future.
It doesn’t have to be that way.
**If you’re able, chip in today to help build a future where Congress rejects war and holds the President accountable. Every dollar donated and every hour volunteered contributes to our campaign for peace and builds momentum heading into the Primary.**

name: James Talarico
subject: Two names you need to know.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Talarico for Texas
body:
#
Peter —
If you want to understand Texas politics and what our movement is up against, then you need to know two names:
**Tim Dunn and Farris Wilks.**
They are two billionaire mega-donors from West Texas. They’re oil and gas oligarchs turned pastors who have bought nearly every right-wing politician in Texas.
And I mean that literally. They bought state government by electing their puppet politicians from state house to governor.
A lot of the most harmful and headline-making legislation that’s come out of Texas is by their decree — the 10 Commandments bill, school vouchers, the abortion ban, and the list goes on. They bought Ken Paxton’s acquittal in the state Senate for $3 million.
**Now they’re trying to install their puppet in the U.S. Senate. And we can’t let that happen.**
Their ultimate goal is even more ambitious: transforming Texas into an authoritarian, Christian Nationalist state. They are buying think tanks and media outlets, and they are turning toward federal races to build an empire that can ultimately take this agenda nationwide.
I know this sounds alarmist, but that is the goal of these billionaire pastors.
I’m well aware that they’re furious about our movement and the threat we pose to their power. Being willing to name them in Texas immediately puts a target on my back. It’s a risk, but we can’t challenge the corrupt status quo by staying silent.
We must speak truth to power. Texas is too big and too great to be sold to the highest bidder.
But I can’t take them on alone.

The United States Postal Service is being pushed toward a financial breaking point. Without Congressional action, the USPS could run out of cash as early as next February. This isn't an accident;_it’s the result of years of bad policy designed to drain the agency and pave the way for greedy corporate privatization._ For the disability community, a privatized or broken Post Office isn't just an inconvenience; it’s a crisis. The USPS is our lifeline. clean_body: | | | The United States Postal Service is being pushed toward a financial breaking point. Without Congressional action, the USPS could run out of cash as early as next February. This isn't an accident;it’s the result of years of bad policy designed to drain the agency and pave the way for greedy corporate privatization. For the disability community, a privatized or broken Post Office isn't just an inconvenience; it’s a crisis. The USPS is our lifeline. We rely on it for the delivery of life-saving medications, the receipt of Social Security documents, and the ability to cast our ballots privately and independently through mail-in voting. We cannot allow our essential services to be sold off piecemeal to the highest bidder. | Privatization means higher costs and service shutdowns that would disproportionately throw people with disabilities under the bus. We are demanding that Congress allow the USPS to fully manage its own funds, adjust borrowing authority for inflation, and offer new revenue-generating services. ** In solidarity, \- Able Dems elects Democrats with disabilities. Today is Election Day. The polls are still open, and across the Commonwealth, votes are being cast on a referendum which, if successful, would give the Democrats the ability to REDRAW the Virginia congressional maps completely in their favor!
When I flipped Virginia's 2nd District RED in 2022, the Democrats were furious. When we won again in 2024 despite their lies, the vandalism of my campaign office, and millions in dark money spent against us, they became desperate. When they realized they could not defeat us fairly, they activated their ultimate backup plan.

They will completely wipe out Republican seats, decimate the entire Republican delegation, and hand the House Majority straight to the radical Left.
This is not just cheating. It is a permanent erasure of your conservative voice.
As a former Navy Helicopter Pilot, I am used to operating under pressure. I did not back down when I flew missions overseas, and I am certainly not backing down from a fight with Washington Democrats who want to strip Southeast Virginia of its commonsense conservative representation.
But I cannot fight their dark money machine alone on Election Day - everything comes down to what happens today.

clean_body: | | Friend, see this photo? That’s me as a kid. = I never thought that I would run for office when I was a little girl — let alone become the first woman governor of New York. When I was born, my parents had just moved out of a trailer and into a small apartment in Woodlawn, New York. My dad worked long shifts at the steel mill. I watched my mother — who raised six kids — stretch every dollar by buying used clothes and serving fried spam sandwiches for dinner. Witnessing the struggles and pain of those left behind inspired me to run for office, to be a voice for communities that had fallen on hard times, because I had lived that experience. I refuse to sit back and watch as these same struggling families are abandoned by Donald Trump, Bruce Blakeman, and their D.C. Republican allies. But Republican special interest donors could rush millions to my opponent, Bruce Blakeman, to buy control of New York. = Friend, my childhood inspired me to fight for New York families with everything I’ve got. unprecedented congressional maneuver to overturn Grand Staircase-Escalante’s
management plan, removing virtually all meaningful protections for the national
monument. The move puts all national monuments at risk. This Earth Day, we need your help. Earth Day is tomorrow and we’ve set a goal of mobilizing 422 people to renew

they can exploit this overreach, time and again to gut protections for our
national monuments and hand over our public lands to corporate polluters. Say NO to Drilling and Mining Near National Monuments This Earth Day!

🎯 The goal: 422 supporters who care about public lands

📅 The deadline: MIDNIGHT on April 22

🚀 The match: 3X until midnight tomorrow

Renew your LCV membership for just $15 to TRIPLE your impact this Earth Day >> https://links.messages.lcv. If this scheme is successful, it won’t just weaken protections for Grand

body:
Our 58 14-ers are a big part of why CO is the most beautiful state in the country. Chip in $14 now to help me keep it that way.
| | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129900595/615930427/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1252-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MTM5ZmI4Ni1iMTNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LN4Mn9AS1DSoX43Hsvv5uLU2YnLC8eMDQ1PH7q404r4=)
Friend,
As a Coloradan and an avid hiker, I take a lot of pride in the fact that we've got more fourteeners (peaks of 14,000 feet or higher in elevation) here in our backyard than in any other state – 58, to be exact.
They're at the heart of our outdoor heritage and economy. They're where some of my most treasured memories have been made. They're part of what makes Colorado, in my not-so-humble opinion, the most beautiful state in the U.S.

**Why ordinary people need AI fluency now -- not to surrender to billionaire-built systems, but to defend human dignity, privacy, work, and the future of consciousness itself.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a8eb1b7c-8600-4dae-a254-e4403c143c16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We are being told two stories about artificial intelligence, and neither one is sufficient.
The first is the corporate story: that AI is inevitable, benevolent, and best left in the hands of the companies building it. Trust the experts. Trust the market. Trust the men who built the platforms that already colonized your attention, rewired your habits, profited from your children's distraction, eroded local journalism, extracted your data, and turned human presence into inventory. This time, they assure us, it will be different.
The second is the purist story: that these tools are irredeemably corrupt, inherently dehumanizing, and best rejected wholesale. Do not touch them. Do not learn them. Do not engage.
I understand why people feel pulled toward both.
The concerns are real. The data centers are real. The energy and water demands are real. The privacy violations are real. The surveillance architecture is real. The billionaire dominance is real. The extraction incentives are real. The job displacement is real. The economic disruption is not theoretical. The temptation to offload too much of our thinking, our memory, our writing, our intimacy, our judgment -- that is real too.
And yet I do not believe refusal, by itself, is a strategy.
Because here is the deeper truth: when powerful systems are being built to mediate knowledge, labor, interpretation, and attention at civilizational scale, opting out does not make you sovereign. It often just makes you dependent on those who opted in first.
That is the part many people are not saying clearly enough.
We are not only dealing with a new productivity tool. We are dealing with a new layer of mediation between human beings and reality. A new class of systems is being built to help decide what we see, what we know, what we trust, what work is valuable, what language sounds competent, what ideas travel, and eventually, which people and institutions can keep up at all.
That means this is not merely a tech issue. It is a power issue. A labor issue. A democracy issue. A sovereignty issue. A soul issue.
**The empire-AI frame**
If that sounds dramatic, look at the pattern.
The same economic class that treated your attention as a mineable resource is now building systems designed to enter more deeply into the interior of human life: your drafts, your questions, your decisions, your fears, your workflows, your private reflections, your style, your intellectual habits, your search for meaning, your need for help, your exhaustion, your uncertainty, your longing to become more capable.
That is not a neutral frontier.
Empire has always sought to map, extract, categorize, discipline, and profit from whatever territory it can reach. Land. Labor. Minerals. Trade routes. Bodies. Culture. Language. Memory.
Now the target is cognitive space itself.
The target is the terrain where perception is shaped. Where desire is nudged. Where habits are trained. Where interpretations are normalized. Where inner life becomes legible to systems designed by actors whose incentives do not align with human flourishing, democratic dignity, or ecological sanity.
That is why I do not think the right response is either naive embrace or frightened refusal.
The right response is disciplined appropriation.
Learn the tools. Understand them. Use them carefully. Teach others. Build norms around them. Refuse the worldview embedded in their default incentives. Redirect them toward human and ecological ends.
This is not capitulation. It is self-defense.
The slogan that gets repeated so often -- that you cannot dismantle the master's house with the master's tools -- is memorable, but historically it is not universally true. Colonized and subordinated peoples have often made real gains not by remaining untouched by dominant systems, but by mastering them without surrendering their own civilizational center.
India did not move toward independence by protecting itself from English, British law, or bureaucratic fluency. Indians of many regions, languages, and traditions learned the language of power, learned the mechanisms of the state, and fought through and within the architecture of empire while remaining animated by something deeper than empire. Native nations, too, have won vital material protections not through romantic distance from the legal order imposed on them, but through extraordinary persistence in treaty law, jurisdictional argument, federal process, record-building, and institutional memory. Not total liberation. But real gains. Real protections. Real survival.
The lesson is not that the master's tools are pure. They are not. The lesson is that a people who refuse all contact with power's instruments often leave those instruments entirely in the hands of their enemies.
That is exactly where we are with AI.
**Why people are uneasy -- and why they should be**
Let us be honest about the fears, because they are not irrational.
People are uneasy because they can feel the scale of what is changing before the public has meaningful consent, governance, or protection.
They are uneasy because enormous data centers are being built while communities worry about water, power, land use, emissions, and fragility. They are uneasy because the same firms asking to mediate the future have a long track record of moving fast while everyone else absorbs the cost.
They are uneasy because privacy is already so broken that many people no longer fully understand how much of their lives is machine-readable.
They are uneasy because surveillance no longer looks only like a camera on a pole. It looks like behavioral inference. It looks like predictive sorting. It looks like quiet ranking systems. It looks like employers, insurers, schools, governments, advertisers, and platforms using synthetic cognition to make more aggressive decisions about human beings.
They are uneasy because they are right to suspect that billionaires do not pour hundreds of billions of dollars into infrastructure because they want ordinary people to become freer, wiser, more politically independent, and less economically exploitable.
They are uneasy because work is changing faster than wages, benefits, retraining, labor law, and public narrative.
And they are uneasy because some of the promised benefits are real enough to be seductive.
That matters too.
AI can, in fact, help people think faster, draft more clearly, learn more broadly, bridge skill gaps, unlock creativity, prototype ideas, navigate bureaucracy, analyze patterns, expand productivity, and reduce friction. It can help a tired parent think through a problem. Help a small business owner do the work of three people. Help an organizer synthesize a mountain of information. Help a writer move through resistance. Help a farmer compare land strategies. Help a volunteer build something useful without waiting for an institution to save them.
The issue is not whether there is genuine amplification here.
There is.
The issue is who gets amplified, under what conditions, toward whose ends, and at what cost.
That is where the conversation usually collapses.
**The false choice**
We are being offered a false choice between passive adoption and total rejection.
But there is a third path.
The third path says: yes, these systems are shaped by extraction incentives. Yes, they are dangerous. Yes, they can deskill, surveil, manipulate, centralize, and distort. Yes, they can be used against workers, against children, against dissent, against truth, against the ecological future.
And because all of that is true, communities need people who actually understand them.
Not hype men. Not corporate evangelists. Not merely "power users" showing off tricks online. Not people whose sole ambition is shaving two minutes off email.
We need a class of practitioners who are technically fluent, ethically serious, culturally rooted, psychologically uncolonized, and oriented toward human dignity rather than platform dependency.
We need AI artisans.
**What I mean by AI artisans**
I do not mean people who worship the machine.
I mean people who know how to work with it without being worked over by it.
People who understand its strengths, its distortions, its blind spots, its failure modes, its seductions, and its incentives.
People who can say to their families, their communities, their congregations, their students, their coworkers, their campaigns, their farms, their local institutions: here is what this can do; here is what it cannot do; here is where it lies; here is where it helps; here is what must never be outsourced; here is how to use it without slowly handing over your interior life.
An AI artisan is not simply a consumer of outputs. An artisan develops judgment.
An artisan notices when a tool is making them faster but shallower. More efficient but less alive. More productive but less sovereign. More fluent but less truthful. More impressive but less original. More dependent but less free.
An artisan can also redirect the tool.
Toward education instead of deskilling. Toward civic literacy instead of mass persuasion. Toward mutual aid instead of manipulative commerce. Toward local resilience instead of total platform dependence. Toward land stewardship instead of abstraction. Toward cultural preservation instead of flattening. Toward real human capability instead of the performance of capability.
That is the cohort we need now.
Not because the models are good.
Because power is real.
**What ordinary people should actually do**
This is the part I care about most.
If we leave AI development, deployment, interpretation, and social normalization entirely to billionaires, venture capital, captured states, and corporate managers, then we should not act surprised when the result is a world optimized for extraction.
If, on the other hand, ordinary people, teachers, mothers, organizers, writers, workers, farmers, ethical technologists, faith communities, local officials, artists, researchers, and civic builders become genuinely fluent in these systems, something else becomes possible.
Not utopia. Not purity. But leverage.
Here is what I think "doing this" actually means.
First, **learn enough to stop being mystified.** You do not need to become an engineer to become harder to manipulate. But you do need to understand the basic behavior of these systems: what they are trained on, how they predict, where they fail, what they retain, what not to share, when to trust, when to verify, and how incentives shape outputs.
Second, **keep your moral center outside the machine.** Do not let a model become your conscience, your oracle, your therapist, your theology, your strategic decider, or your substitute for contact with the real. Use it as an instrument. Do not crown it.
Third, **use AI to build human capability, not replace it.** Use it to strengthen writing, not eliminate the need to think. Use it to accelerate learning, not erase craft. Use it to widen participation, not concentrate expertise further. Use it to scaffold competence in people who are under-resourced, overworked, or excluded from elite systems.
Fourth, **create local knowledge and practice communities**. People should not be navigating this alone. We need circles, workshops, guilds, parent groups, worker groups, homeschool groups, farmer groups, faith communities, and civic groups where people can share patterns, norms, cautions, use cases, and protective practices.
Fifth, **fight for boundaries**. Not everything should be uploaded. Not every process should be automated. Not every decision should be machine-assisted. Not every child should be trained into synthetic dependency. Not every employer should be allowed to surveil cognition under the language of productivity. Not every public institution should procure these systems without transparency, contestability, and democratic oversight.
Sixth, **develop alternatives where possible**. Community-owned datasets. Smaller, lower-energy models for specific local tasks. Privacy-respecting workflows. Open tools where appropriate. Human review structures. Offline or limited-exposure use cases. Domain-specific applications rooted in actual community benefit rather than abstract scale.
Seventh, **tie AI use back to material life.** If your use of AI does not make you more capable of caring for real people, doing better work, building stronger institutions, defending truth, stewarding land, preserving memory, or increasing democratic agency, then what exactly is it doing to you?
That question should haunt us more than it currently does.
**The danger on both sides**
There is a danger in the corporate embrace of AI.
But there is also a danger in elite-coded refusal.
A politics that tells ordinary people to stay away from powerful tools can become, in practice, a politics of managed helplessness.
It can leave the field to those already best positioned to dominate it.
Meanwhile the people who most need leverage -- workers, dissidents, small institutions, marginalized communities, overstretched parents, local journalists, independent researchers, grassroots campaigns, ethical entrepreneurs -- are told to keep their hands clean while the architecture of the future is built around them.
No.
That is not a serious answer.
But there is another danger too: not everyone who learns these tools will use them well. Some will become more efficient servants of extraction. Some will become polished rationalizers of surveillance. Some will become manipulators with better language. Some will become middle managers of machine-shaped life.
Technical fluency does not automatically produce liberation.
It can just as easily produce a new comprador class: people close enough to power to benefit from it, far enough from principle to excuse it, and skilled enough to make domination look modern.
That is why training alone is not enough.
What we need is formation.
Formation in ethics. Formation in democratic values. Formation in spiritual seriousness. Formation in attention. Formation in labor solidarity. Formation in what human beings are for. Formation in what should never be optimized away. Formation in ecological reality. Formation in the difference between intelligence and wisdom.
Without that, we are just producing better adapters to empire.
With it, we may be able to produce defenders.
**A better question than "should we use AI?"**
The question is no longer whether these systems will exist in public life.
They already do.
The better question is this:
Who will become fluent enough to shape how they are used, constrained, interpreted, resisted, and redirected?
And in service of what?
Will AI remain primarily a tool of concentrated capital, managerial sorting, cognitive capture, and polite social deskilling?
Or will enough people learn to work with it in ways that increase public capability, defend privacy, preserve interiority, strengthen local institutions, widen access to craft, and keep human judgment alive at the center of the process?
That is not a software question. That is a political question. A moral question. A civilizational question.
And it will not be answered for us by the market.
**My position**
I do not trust billionaire-built systems to shepherd the human future. I do not trust extraction incentives to produce dignity by accident. I do not trust centralized infrastructures of cognition to remain benign merely because their interfaces are friendly. I do not trust the people who colonized our attention to suddenly become guardians of our minds.
But I also do not believe the answer is to back away from the tools altogether while those same actors move deeper into governance, labor, education, media, and daily life.
We need disciplined people who can enter this terrain without becoming owned by it.
We need communities that can use these systems without worshipping them.
We need practitioners who can translate between machine capability and moral reality.
We need people who can help others become more capable, not more dependent.
We need to build enough literacy, enough norms, enough infrastructure, enough courage, and enough shared language that the future of synthetic cognition is not determined solely by those who see human consciousness as a monetizable surface.
That is the work.
Learn the tools. Master them carefully. Teach others. Draw boundaries. Protect what is sacred. Build what is local. Refuse what is extractive. Keep your judgment alive. Keep your humanity intact. Keep your allegiance with life.
Because the empire does want your mind.
And that is exactly why you cannot afford to leave the tools entirely in its hands.

This lab helps scientists predict hurricanes, wildfires, floods, and extreme weather events that threaten communities across our country. But instead of listening to scientists, this administration is attacking them.

This is part of a pattern we’ve seen again and again: undermine research, silence experts, and pretend facts don’t matter. **I’m Dr. Jasmine Clark. I have a PhD in microbiology. I’ve spent my career studying science, teaching science, and fighting for evidence-based solutions to the challenges our communities face.**
