body:
Friend,

Yesterday, Senator Chris Murphy saw a report that Iran had broken
through a U.S. blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. His response? He
typed "awesome" and hit send.

When the backlash came, he claimed it was sarcasm. Maybe it was. But
here's what matters: a sitting U.S. Senator's first instinct when he
thought Iran had beaten America was to celebrate.

My father hid our family in a fishing boat to escape Vietnam in 1985.
Three days at sea. He knew what happens when authoritarian regimes win
and America looks weak. We didn't risk everything to come here so that
U.S. Senators could root for our enemies.

Derek Tran is part of the same Democratic caucus that produces Chris
Murphys. The same party that opposed the Trump Administration's strike
on Iranian nuclear facilities. The same Democrats who co-signed a War
Powers Resolution to tie the President's hands against Iran.

Tran won CA-45 by just 653 votes. 653. That margin is the only thing
standing between a district that believes America should win and a
Congressman who votes with people who think Iran breaking through our
blockade is "awesome."

I'm running because I remember what it cost to get here. I remember
what my father risked. And I will never — not once, not as a joke,
not as sarcasm — celebrate when America's enemies win.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Western Slope farmers lit fires to [protect orchards from a sudden freeze](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after early warm weather, while Lone Tree officials [push back on state laws](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) they say undermine local zoning control. Scrutiny is also increasing around a CPW nominee and the broader [authority of the governor-appointed board](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over wildlife and land-use decisions. Finally, potential federal Medicaid cuts could strain hospitals, including [several in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Federal officials report hundreds of thousands of [ineligible names on voter rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as DOJ enforcement efforts expand, while Democrats discuss [adding new states and expanding the Supreme Court](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Broader commentary highlights concerns about governance, [trust](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and [preserving constitutional principles](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) rooted in the nation’s founding.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, April 21, 2026.

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado murder bill advances: Sentencing cuts collide with voter mandate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado voters approved [Proposition 128](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in November 2024 with 62 percent support, requiring those convicted of second-degree murder and several other violent felonies to serve at least 85 percent of their sentence before becoming eligible for parole.
Seventeen months later, [House Bill 26-1281](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is headed to the House floor. While much of the debate has focused on how the bill treats completed murders, most of its effect may come from how it changes penalties for attempted cases — incidents far more common in Colorado.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[Patriots Day: Remembering the Courage That Built America](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY REP. SCOTT BOTTOMS, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Patriots’ Day honors citizen-led defense of liberty:** The holiday commemorates the 1775 battles of Lexington and Concord, where ordinary Americans stood against British forces, emphasizing that freedom was worth defending.
* **Founding principles centered on limited government:** The commentary highlights that the Revolution was driven by concerns over government overreach, with the belief that rights come from the people and government exists to protect them—not grant them.
* **Modern relevance tied to civic responsibility:** The piece argues those same principles still apply today, stressing the importance of local control, citizen engagement, and vigilance to preserve liberty and self-government.

* **CPW nominee faces questions over past statements and transparency:** Concerns have been raised about statements attributed to nominee Christopher Sichko regarding “rewilding” the Great Plains, with questions about whether those views reflect his current positions and why related content may no longer be publicly available.
* **Unelected board’s influence under scrutiny:** The Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission—made up of gubernatorial appointees—is facing broader criticism over its growing role in shaping wildlife and land-use policy without direct voter accountability.
* **Activist-driven policy proposals raise concerns:** Recent petitions and advocacy efforts, including proposals affecting hunting practices, are cited as examples of how outside groups may influence policy decisions through the commission, prompting debate over transparency and public input.

It’s one of my favorites, especially because I recently shared it with my grandchild. That special moment truly highlighted for me how this lovely rhyme reflects a kind of leadership—a wonderful kind at that—The Art of War, Jesus Style._

Not because of a storm. Not because of a staffing shortage. Because a cyberattack forced it to. “They had to block Stryker from coming into their network and cancel all of the surgeries that required that robotic device,” said Maria Orms, a cybersecurity professional who was a gubernatorial candidate at the April 11 assembly. “That could cause someone to die.”_

I’ll be the first to admit, I'm not your typical candidate.
You might actually recognize me from TV — and no, not from a campaign ad.
In December 2023, I walked onto the Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard stage as a Marine Corps Intelligence Officer stationed in Stuttgart, Germany. Heading into Final Jeopardy, I had a lead, a category I liked, and a decision to make.
I bet everything...
... and I was right.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
That's how I approach most things in life. You do your homework, you back your judgment, and you don't flinch when the stakes are high.
Right now, the stakes couldn't be higher — and I'm asking you to back me as I take on my next challenge: Running for Congress.
My name is Tyler Vandenberg, and I'm a Democrat running for Congress in California's 6th District. I'm a Harvard Kennedy School graduate, a former Marine officer, and a proud Californian who has spent his career serving this country and our democracy. Now, I’m coming home to fight for it.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or even $100 today to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to help us WIN? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP WIN THIS RACE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
I didn't come to this decision lightly. After the 2024 election, I watched MAGA Extremists launch attack after attack on everything I love about this state and this country. Cuts to wildland firefighters. Slashing Medicaid. Threatening to sell off our National Forests. Gutting the agencies that keep our communities safe and our air and water clean.
And then there's Kevin Kiley — my opponent, the man currently occupying this seat.
Kiley has recently tried to rebrand himself as an "independent."
Don't believe it for a second.
Kevin Kiley votes with Donald Trump virtually every single time. The independent label is a costume he's trying on because he knows his record is a liability. He's not independent. He's MAGA with crafty branding.
California's 6th deserves better. And I intend to deliver it.
Here's what I'm going to fight for when I get to Congress:
I'm going to fight to make California affordable again. Housing costs are crushing working families across this district. I'll push for real solutions — more housing supply, stronger tenant protections, and federal investment in the infrastructure that makes communities livable. The cost of living isn't a talking point to me. I worked two restaurant jobs just to make rent when I was starting out. I know what it means to hustle just to get by.
I'm going to fight to protect our public lands and our environment. The GOP wants to sell off our National Forests. I want to protect them, fund them, and keep them accessible to every Californian — not just the wealthy few who can afford what comes after privatization. California's wilderness is not for sale.
I'm going to fight to defend Social Security and Medicare. These aren't government handouts — they're promises this country made to working people. I'll oppose any effort to cut, privatize, or undermine them, full stop.
I'm going to fight to protect our neighbors. Immigrants, women, and LGBTQ+ Californians are under assault from this administration. That ends when we flip this seat.
And I'm going to hold MAGA accountable. Not just with speeches — with votes, with investigations, with every tool available to a Member of Congress. The era of consequence-free MAGA corruption has to end somewhere. It can end here.
I spent years in the Marine Corps learning that servant leadership isn't a slogan — it's a discipline. It means showing up, doing the hard work, and putting the people you serve ahead of yourself. That's the kind of congressman I intend to be.
I'm not coming to Washington to build a brand or further my own career.
I'm coming to do the job.
But I need your help to get there. Races like this one don't flip themselves. They flip because people like you decide early that it's worth fighting for — and put their money where their values are.
So, can I count on you to chip in to my campaign TODAY? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
CHIP IN TO HELP DEMS RETAKE THE HOUSE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
Every dollar goes directly toward building the campaign that beats Kevin Kiley and sends California's 6th a representative who actually works for them.
Let's get to work.
— Tyler Vandenberg

name: Sarah McBride
subject: What I told Jon Lovett
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
I recently had the chance to chat with Jon Lovett on Pod Save America, and I want to share what I told him with you.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3140%2E21716%2E3784uq)
I recently had the chance to chat with Jon Lovett on Pod Save America, and I want to share what I told him with you.
When MAGA Republicans pull crazy stunts or lash out in an attempt to get on Fox News or in your social media feeds, they’re doing it because they’re addicted to the high of going viral.
**When we refuse to react — refuse to give them the attention they’re seeking — we can deny them that high and keep the focus on the real work that Congress is supposed to be doing.**
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260421-1.IOPpsp&refcode=em20260421-3140&t=2&akid=3140%2E21716%2E3784uq)
When I first came to Congress last year, MAGA Republicans tried their hardest to get a reaction out of me by targeting me over my identity.
Instead of giving them the attention they were seeking, I did what my neighbors in Delaware elected me to do. I stayed focused on improving the lives of working families up and down our state.
Now, a little over a year later, I’ve introduced more pieces of bipartisan legislation than any other freshman Member of Congress. It may not get the kind of viral attention that MAGA Republicans are seeking, but that’s how we get real work done.
And I know there’s such potential to do more good if we can take back the House this November. But I’m counting on your support to do it — starting with defending my seat.
[**If you’re with me, will you donate $5 or any amount today to support my campaign and help me keep up the work I’m doing in Congress?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260421-1.IOPpsp&refcode=em20260421-3140&amount=5&t=3&akid=3140%2E21716%2E3784uq)

Thank you,
Sarah McBride

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

It's a shame we live in a time where this even needs to be discussed. It's common knowledge that a mother's role in a child's life is integral to the healthy development of that child. To intentionally faciliate that depravation is nothing short of a crime against the children of America. Which is why on my first day in Congress, I will introduce legislation banning surrogacy for single men and same-sex couples. The rest of the world has banned it and it's time for America to catch up, and do the same. Grit and heart at the Michigan Democratic Convention

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oYWxleWZvcm1pLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.065dN1lAvxDnoNoWddiegUE2ljNpYFwUW9Bjiq9zYYg?) for more

# [I'm never going to stop fighting](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=194555674&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0NTU1Njc0LCJpYXQiOjE3NzY3OTk2MTAsImV4cCI6MTc3OTM5MTYxMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.TGjxLX_EYOD2jDOtVVjpuG8tIvbecPYa4crl7TElQq4)
### Grit and heart at the Michigan Democratic Convention
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Apr 21
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..HH7Urtz09MADzOjaH1NuJpro5Lz6d0YLdg7AFgQLrDs?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/earlier-today-i-stepped-onto-the?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

**This weekend I attended the Michigan Democratic Convention.**
As I connected with folks in each caucus room - the Michiganders who had come from across the state - I felt so proud. I felt energized. And I felt really, really grateful.
Because when you stand in a room full of people who care this deeply about Michigan - people who have given their time, their energy, their weekends, their hope - it reminds you who politics is supposed to be about.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/856512b3-ff46-4f46-8c51-0786d65619c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
These folks weren't high-paid consultants or MAGA billionaires trying to buy themselves another tax break. This convention was made up of teachers, nurses, union members, and people who were ready to stand together and make our state better.
**Sure, they 're worried about high gas prices, health care, and the future of our country - but they still showed up.**
[That's Michigan grit.](https://substack.com/redirect/b331c0ee-81df-491e-bfc4-081cf9f9cac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And I love it so much.
I met so many good people over the past few days. People who encouraged me. People who told me their stories. People who reminded me why I got into this work in the first place.
And in our battleground race, that matters more than ever.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02a50417-85a2-44a7-bd8c-8d3807ee8a23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You can tell how important this state is by who showed up this weekend. Kamala Harris, Cory Booker, and Andy Beshear all spoke to local Democratic groups connected to the convention. That's not random. **[Leaders across the country understand that what happens in Michigan matters- not just here, but for the future of the Senate.](https://substack.com/redirect/b331c0ee-81df-491e-bfc4-081cf9f9cac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
It was beautiful to see the spotlight shine on this place I love. And it sharpened my focus.
Folks, this battleground race is not abstract. It is not some game for cable news to cover like the Pistons' playoff run.
**There are real Michiganders whose lives will be affected by what happens in this race.**
It is about whether the people of Michigan have a senator who wakes up every day thinking about workers, families, farms, factories, and small businesses - and whether regular folks can actually afford to live.
It is about whether the people who built this state have somebody in the Senate who will fight for them or whether this seat gets handed over to Mike Rogers and the MAGA billionaires trying to buy it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22a1eede-cbf8-403e-9b20-caad1e82f343?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Last week, another poll came out showing me leading my primary opponents - now the eighth poll showing us ahead. That matters.**
It tells me that people can see what this campaign is about. They know that I'm fighting for Michigan's working families, for our farmers, our teachers and our labor communities.
But I'm not naive about what we're up against.
_The New York Times_ reported this month that the Senate Leadership Fund, a Republican super PAC, is planning to spend $45 million in Michigan, making us the No. 1 target among Democratic-held seats. Far-right, anti-abortion groups are already running ads attacking me.
That should tell you everything.
Republicans know Michigan is critical. They know Senate control will run straight through this state. [And they are preparing to spend whatever it takes to try to flip this seat.](https://substack.com/redirect/b331c0ee-81df-491e-bfc4-081cf9f9cac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**So today, I felt both things at once: the joy of this moment and the stakes of what we 're up against.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c861ab7e-e1a2-42df-ba1a-50758faad349?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We can win this race. I know it in my bones.
Because this state is full of people who care. The Michiganders I met this weekend work hard, believe in their communities, and believe government ought to work for regular families - not just MAGA billionaires and their rightwing politicians.
That's who I'm standing with.
That's who I'm fighting for. And nothing is going to stop me.
With grit,
Haley
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/716af1fb-2fcd-4f02-b484-ec524345dc05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/b331c0ee-81df-491e-bfc4-081cf9f9cac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Peter, we want to share a bit about Jen Jordan’s story, and why [we’re asking for your help today by splitting a donation between the Democratic Party of Georgia and Jen’s campaign for the Georgia Supreme Court.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129903918/615941504/-94870376?&amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_042126_B1_JENJORDAN_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZTA2MWM4NS1iODNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GRwX0jawqfh5m0HVE3edz1KwR-Sz587obXavMKuGj_s=) Jen’s story started at a kitchen table in Dodge County, with her single mom who worked as a hairdresser. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129903924/615941514/-94870376?&amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_042126_B1_JENJORDAN_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZTA2MWM4NS1iODNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GRwX0jawqfh5m0HVE3edz1KwR-Sz587obXavMKuGj_s=) Jen’s mom showed her what real perseverance looks like. But she also taught her something just as important: **that hard work needs to be met with a fair shot.** Those early lessons are why Jen became a lawyer. They’re why she served in the Georgia State Senate. They’re why she’s always fought for people who need someone in their corner. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129903931/615941521/-94870376?&amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_042126_B1_JENJORDAN_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZTA2MWM4NS1iODNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GRwX0jawqfh5m0HVE3edz1KwR-Sz587obXavMKuGj_s=) Now, let us tell you about the case that changed everything for her. Jen represented a young woman who survived a horrific sexual assault. A jury heard her story, believed her, and awarded her damages. They did the right thing. Then, the Georgia Supreme Court took it away: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129903938/615941527/-94870376?&amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_042126_B1_JENJORDAN_D1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZTA2MWM4NS1iODNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GRwX0jawqfh5m0HVE3edz1KwR-Sz587obXavMKuGj_s=) The court overturned the jury’s decision, siding with a powerful, well-connected defendant over a survivor. In that moment, that decision sent a dangerous message: **that the system can be used to protect the powerful and silence victims.** That’s the system Jen is running to change. Jen is running against an elitist establishment that protects its own. She’s running to stand up to the corporations and billionaires who act like the rules don’t apply to them — the kind of people who operate with total impunity. She’s running for that survivor, for every woman and girl, and for every Georgian who believes justice should be blind, not bought. The election on May 19th is our chance to choose a different path. It’s our chance to say, **ENOUGH.** **ENOUGH** of courts that find loopholes for the connected.
**ENOUGH** of a status quo that fails victims.
**ENOUGH** of injustice. But to win, we need to build a movement that reaches every voter in Georgia with a simple truth: **our courts must protect people, not power.** [Peter, will you stand with Jen Jordan in this fight? Dear Friends,In case my first announcement letter was missed, I wanted you to know that I officially filed to seek re-election—because the work we’ve started for Michigan’s 30th Senate District is not finished.West Michigan isn’t just where I serve—it’s home. It’s where we raise our families, build our businesses, and invest in our future. That’s why I’ve fought to protect what makes our communities strong while delivering real, measurable results for the people who live here.I’ve supported legislation to bring more medical professionals to Michigan, expanded funding for school safety and mental health services, and invested in safer, more reliable roads and bridges. I’ve also fought for meaningful tax relief—working to lower taxes on tips, overtime pay, and Social Security—so more of your hard-earned money stays where it belongs: with you.I know families are still feeling the pressure of high prices. High prices on things considered necessities. That’s why I’m focused every day on cutting costs where we can, making government more efficient, and eliminating wasteful spending—because Lansing should be working for you, not the other way around.Some candidates run on promises. I can run on results. My record reflects working on and accomplishing the priorities I’ve heard directly from you—through conversations, meetings, and time spent in communities across our district.If re-elected, I will continue to work with anyone—Republican or Democrat—who is serious about getting things done. Together, we can strengthen our economy, restore excellence in education, respect taxpayers, protect seniors, honor our veterans, and create more opportunity for every person, every family, who lives in the 30th Senate District and Michigan.For those that have voted for me in the past, I hope I’ve earned your continued support. For those who are new to the district, I will work hard to gain their trust - and their vote - as I travel the 30th sharing my vision and plans for the upcoming term.To learn more about me please feel free to visit my campaign site: [https://votehuizenga.com](https://brightsparkstrategies.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f3a7dccdb3ca90c7483cf93d3&id=2bd3098c95&e=9ec31248a9)
With gratitude,
**Mark Huizenga**
State Senator, 30th District

I’ve also fought for meaningful tax relief—working to lower taxes on tips, overtime pay, and Social Security—so more of your hard-earned money stays where it belongs: with you.I know families are still feeling the pressure of high prices. High prices on things considered necessities. That’s why I’m focused every day on cutting costs where we can, making government more efficient, and eliminating wasteful spending—because Lansing should be working for you, not the other way around.Some candidates run on promises. I can run on results. My record reflects working on and accomplishing the priorities I’ve heard directly from you—through conversations, meetings, and time spent in communities across our district.If re-elected, I will continue to work with anyone—Republican or Democrat—who is serious about getting things done. Together, we can strengthen our economy, restore excellence in education, respect taxpayers, protect seniors, honor our veterans, and create more opportunity for every person, every family, who lives in the 30th Senate District and Michigan.For those that have voted for me in the past, I hope I’ve earned your continued support. For those who are new to the district, I will work hard to gain their trust - and their vote - as I travel the 30th sharing my vision and plans for the upcoming term.To learn more about me please feel free to visit my campaign site: With gratitude, Mark Huizenga State Senator, 30th District | | | Thank You! Your efforts are truly impactful. By contributing, you’re helping us advocate for the changes and reforms our community needs. Every donation, no matter the size, fuels our mission and ensures a brighter future for all. Patriot,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**
---
[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=8f6ca0bd80c9425587de3a2c5f68d781&_e=iYSGyWfz1ALAEBorXm6Kdc8wrEpbQ-5hJkLcN5af5wtGR_FE6Wad5V1k4IbDLWnw2jMUG-wQ3XGeFGQcKRzMqZM9BnSlNYujUHxmXdeFKKlL0US2e-5hb_42QBzXRMvKNw3Q0MPeODYlo3nQ2vD5GtVVICEuls0byA7Wl3XsMLVJrEg1_l5Ggctginu1AKqXsvT-UEBFfZoIF7CZj9KBxVZdmKJ3_-Z_PnVJ9BCbUJhpDglz2sU3YWcNHI4_wWE8SKs9BiFz9pT8sGEoCJKdExa6ziyeW6m8Gj5pGtmi2IVSpEe-_az-6qCAuI3g1naNi30TRLtIhbnj05RUikseiGqUgae0K-C8FO6n2u9T0VeLsQ878s597OW2icNusbYJVtUX1gdTpmVMwYFgpny0WZYzGtkYUc-7G4t9KxZZKshht-rRNxJjewg3CuSOX2f7qBzcTQm66lNysmiJvzlzddeDFDIDJ6ndCpq0WE-_pW3CYtp3E0ATZ1hcMTNE-uTxPdA-Lgb_QBzH31l97TcuIWili-WOE1L9G0pFfLDcDnOvx1RP9poVaKh0IczzUjSECS1srLt88PHjpr5R8z00bHGtupeTMKvxvxk0AGNnxQWrQ23MQq1cLRU7HEKn2wtVVI6YxSARb0pX40akDjPj2CeHLhzZ1qqis6XcaZhqM9bdmy0GyL-4jDF1VCe_9wfF)

You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. When I held a town hall in Tremont back in January, it was clear that the federal government had no business building warehouse detention centers here. But our leaders kept telling us to sit on our hands and do nothing.
They didn't listen, but that didn't stop us. And every day our coalition gets bigger and our "No" gets louder.
Now two environmental organizations have filed legal challenges to Berks and Schuylkill ICE detention warehouses.
They share our concerns about how these facilities would overwhelm local sewage and water systems, **which could lead to raw waste leaking into the streets and people potentially being denied drinking water.**
Once again, it's not our representative in Washington stepping up to protect us. It's our communities, our neighbors, and now environmental groups who are forced to do our congressman's job for him.
People here know what's at stake. We look out for our neighbors, and we don't accept being told to deal with it. If Dan Meuser won't fight for us, we'll fight for ourselves.

Here’s just a glimpse of what we’re seeing right now:

In Texas, voters broke records by casting 2.3 million votes in the Democratic gubernatorial primary. Voters are tired of MAGA Republicans, and they delivered a decisive primary victory for EMILYs List-endorsed candidate **Gina Hinojosa** (TX-GOV).

In Florida, Democrats flipped two Republican-held seats, including a state House district that includes Trump’s Mar-a-Lago. Those wins are a sign that Trump’s agenda is becoming a political liability, even in his own backyard.

And in Wisconsin, a state Trump won in 2024, **Judge Chris Taylor** won her Supreme Court race by a 20-point margin — nearly _double_ the margin in the state's Supreme Court election last year. We’re working with candidates like Chris all over the country: bold leaders ready to meet the moment.

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: What I saw on the MDP Convention floor is deeply troubling
body:
|
#
Friend, I'm the only Michigan Democrat who won a Trump district in 2024. I know how hard it is to win, and serving in the Minority, I know the consequences of losing. Both losing elections and losing sight of what matters and what unites us. What I saw on the MDP Convention floor is deeply troubling – for what it says about who we are, how we win, and whether we will be able to meet this urgent moment. **Here are my thoughts – and our path forward:** First and foremost, enthusiasm is great, but too much of the behavior we saw on the floor is not acceptable. We need to be able to disagree while treating one another with dignity and respect. We don’t name-call. We don’t belittle and bully. We don’t shout people down. We don’t make them feel unwelcome or unsafe based on who they are. We reject all forms of hate, including both antisemitism and Islamophobia. **We will never beat MAGA by practicing their division. We win by being the opposite.** And while we nominated many leaders with whom I am excited to run this fall, the Convention nominated others with extreme positions and records — like calling Tucker Carlson “a real one,” Hezbollah leaders “martyrs,” or amplifying Qasem Soleimani — that are out of step with my values and those of Democrats across our state. All of this drives one devastating outcome: making it much, much harder for us to win back power this November. But don’t take it from me, take it from MAGA electeds and strategists who cheered on what they saw – because they know it makes their jobs easier. name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision →
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.
Hey folks, it’s Mark Kelly.
Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.
I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.
So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.
I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.
I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.
After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.
**[I’m asking you to split a donation between Chris Pappas and me. We’re going to do everything we can to take back Congress this November, and Chris Pappas needs your help. I just hope you know that I wouldn’t be asking if this wasn’t important.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260421_2.XZV9ao&amount=5&refcode=em20260421-2&t=1&akid=6233%2E582294%2EMGCsGM)**

Thank you.
Mark

# [Tell Chief Justice Roberts: "Stop the Secret Rulings. The Court Must Explain Its Decisions, Dammit."](https://default.salsalabs.org/Te8a67b67-626d-4287-9485-47634116594f/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| | | [](https://default.salsalabs.org/T51d92075-9071-49ee-a42b-8163008b0fca/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) _([Go directly to petition](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4df14e74-a8c7-459a-8c91-0f05f7c4cbbf/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) | [More actions here](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tc3efe3aa-ac59-4db3-acd5-18f2a1b29290/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) [)](https://default.salsalabs.org/Ta732fab5-8088-4c17-9126-9fbd5444cfe3/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)_ In recent years, the Supreme Court has increasingly relied on its so-called "shadow docket" to make major decisions—often late at night, with little explanation, no full briefing, and no oral arguments. It's a terrible practice, as it leaves the nation with no clue as to what drove the decision, and basically lets the Court do whatever the hell it wants, without any legal or Constitutional justification. We're supposed to just "trust them." And now we find out that Chief Justice John Roberts was the one who [made this happen](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tb27a7ac3-0909-41f3-ab43-19306152f89a/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) — going full activist on a series of decisions, without even the pretense of judging the case fairly, and doing it all without the any public justification. What a dick. These aren't minor procedural rulings. They've affected immigration policy, reproductive rights, environmental protections, and more—impacting millions of people without the transparency or accountability Americans expect from the highest court in the land. [**Tell Chief Justice Roberts: "Stop the Secret Rulings. The Court Must Explain Its Decisions, Dammit."**](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tad70fc38-e918-4252-a355-a180186b27dc/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

We're supposed to just "trust them." And now we find out that Chief Justice John Roberts was the one who — going full activist on a series of decisions, without even the pretense of judging the case fairly, and doing it all without the any public justification. subject: “This is NOT supposed to be a close race!”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
MAGA is shocked we're competitive. A Black farmer from rural Louisiana isn't supposed to threaten their Senate seat. But here we are.
| | | | | [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FRmAnlYC68m-C-zhWfrePSTFnYJA4lzLfe3mdpxma2RNcRZMN0pJ9g0z6G_jncBR4JAc4FaZIM_lJGrYcUV_iBdKPdbKW71QUsy9egRHySGyPnXZ0znezaVXaluZIq3rrlE3w4LdBRaDBXWHgjxGW-cOluhCsCby1RrxeYw3M79siODkWy-bRunwC_oEaHxKANH00oS44pXTMMdHXV2ya2Pse5Mb4GAi&c=NqDn86HWKDDz2I5omuYuzMg1VKVlMYFWMZyBCLjU3GMC6d-hptxWjA==&ch=miqgDM8wWAKLJw0S0w5V54pYZG8aGMIvZ8oa9F7Vauk1nmPMklsBpw==)

Peter, Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
And MAGA is absolutely shocked.
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours -- a real populist challenge to their grip on power -- wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
And I believe -- deep in my bones -- that I'm the candidate to meet this moment.
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars -- the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment -- if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable -- everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.

Friend, Big Tech oligarchs are trying to reshape our country. They’re rapidly expanding unregulated data centers, which consume massive amounts of water, dirty energy, and land. For example, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is planning a data center the size of Manhattan. Oracle and OpenAI CEOs are pushing through a data center near my community that will use millions of gallons of water daily and as much energy as 1 million homes. Communities near data centers are suffering from extremely loud noise pollution and toxic pollution of their air, water, and soil. Their utility rates have gone way up to make up for data centers’ strain on the electric grid, with increases as high as 270 percent. Americans already struggle to pay for the basics. Data centers are making our lives more expensive, all so billionaires can accumulate more wealth and power. That’s why **I’m supporting new legislation in Congress, which would impose a moratorium to pause new development of AI data centers.** [**Please click here to watch my remarks at a recent rally Plus, they’re powering artificial intelligence (AI), which steals from artists, violates our privacy, drives anti-democratic misinformation and bots, and is set to eliminate millions of jobs. Larry Ellison said of AI-powered surveillance: “citizens will be on their best behavior because we are constantly recording and reporting everything that’s going on.” We need a nationwide moratorium on data centers now. That’s why I’m supporting the** Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Moratorium Act, which would end data centers’ expansion until strong safeguards for AI and data centers are put in place to protect communities, workers, and our planet. Corporations and Republican lawmakers are trying to build these massive, polluting centers near lower-income communities and communities of color. Tech billionaires Larry Ellison of Oracle and Sam Altman of OpenAI are pushing through a data center near my majority-minority congressional district. After intense community pushback and the Saline Township’s board voting to stop it, the project’s developer sued the township. Now, Michigan’s first hyper-scale data center is under construction there. It will use as much energy as 1 million homes, and gobble up millions of gallons of water a day—all so billionaires can personally profit from AI at our expense. The American people don’t want this. A strong people-powered movement across the country has delayed or cancelled between a third and a half of data centers planned for 2026. Over 100 U.S. communities have enacted moratoriums or bans on data centers, and statewide moratoriums have been introduced in 12 states—including bipartisan policies in my home state of Michigan. But Republicans and billionaires are trying to override and undermine community opposition. They’re fighting against much-needed industry regulation. We can’t let them silence us. To truly represent all the Americans saying “hell no” to data centers, we need federal protections for all states and communities. Thank you for taking action. I promise to continue holding Big Tech and corporate polluters accountable, and fighting for environmental, racial, and economic justice. I’m also a cosponsor of the Data Center Community Impact Act , to begin a federal study of AI data centers’ impacts on public health, the economy, the environment, the electric grid, and our communities—particularly impacts on communities of color and lower-income communities, which are already disproportionately exposed to pollution. With you in the fight for our rights, Rashida Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via . subject: We need to start showing up again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
I’ve spent enough time in politics to know this: when Democrats stop
showing up in certain places, somebody else fills the void.

Usually, it’s people who have no real interest in helping working families
— just dividing them, distracting them, and cashing in while communities
get left behind. After a while, that kind of politics takes a toll. People
start feeling like nobody sees them, nobody hears them, and nobody is
fighting for the places they call home.

I think there’s a better path.

It starts by taking small towns seriously. It starts by respecting people
enough to tell the truth. And it starts by showing up, organizing, and
competing in places too many folks in politics have given up on. That’s a
big part of why I’m launching Small Town PAC.

Small Town PAC is about helping Democrats expand the map by building power
in small towns and backing the kind of politics that actually speak to
working families. Because if we want to win in more places, we’ve got to
be willing to show up in more places.

That’s the work ahead, and I’m asking you to be part of it from the start.

I knew it was going to be a good day yesterday at UT Arlington.
Some stand out moments:
Meeting aerospace engineering major Aixa as she’s holding her laser cut rocket with printed parts that she designed on CAD.
Evelyn who at 22 got registered for the first time, and when I asked her why she said I saw you all working so hard over here and thought maybe there’s something to this.
Peter who is in the national guard and finishing his studies at UTA. Dedicated to this country and wants to do more to make sure we come out alright.
Jackson who worries that too many Democrats would “rather do nothing wrong than something right,” echoed by many of his fellow students who want to see leadership, action, change.
Vanessa, taking graduation pictures, just finished her criminal justice degree, going to law school next.
And Belén a high school senior who is touring the campus with her mom as she chooses between St. Edward’s and UTA.
Our incredible organizers and volunteers helped more than 270 students get registered, update their registration or confirm their registration today — and in all cases we will personally stay in touch to answer questions about voting, protect their voting status and make sure they vote!

body:
These elections will shape everyday life for countless Americans.
Peter,

Recently, Gov. Andy Beshear spoke with Rev. Al Sharpton about something that doesn't always get enough attention: The 36 governors' races happening right now across the country.

While a lot of the focus is on Washington, it's often governors who are making the decisions that shape people's everyday lives. In many states, a strong Democratic governor is the last line of defense against this administration's most harmful policies.

**Democratic Governors influence state budgets, deciding where state resources go. They attract major employers and companies to set up shop in the state, bringing good-paying jobs. And they have the power to push back on overreach from the federal government.**

Andy has always stayed focused on putting the needs of Kentuckians first. That's not just good for Kentuckians, who get a governor focused on providing high-paying jobs, better access to healthcare, and great public education—it's also good politics. When Andy ran for governor _and won twice in deep-red Kentucky,_ it was because he talked about what people were actually going through every single day.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: These are the words that have guided my work to fight for all Texans.
body:
Now I’m taking this lesson with me in this fight to beat Greg Abbott in November.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I often think about something my grandmother used to tell me:
_“No te dejes.”_
Don’t let them push you around. Fight back.
That lesson has guided me my entire life — and it’s why**I’m running for Governor of Texas.**
Because right now, Texans are in the fight of our lives for our kids, our schools, and our future. **And Greg Abbott has chosen a side: the billionaires, the special interests, the corporations, and the wealthiest donors who bankroll him.**
Abbott has spent nearly a billion dollars in taxpayer money on his campaign donors and is still scheming to rip funding away from our neighborhood public schools to give to private interests.**That’s corruption, plain and simple — _and it’s time we fought back_.**
If you’re ready to take our state back from Abbott and his billionaire donors, I have to ask:
[**Will you donate $5 to my campaign to have enough resources to reach Texans, share my message with them, and prove we’re ready for this fight against Greg Abbott’s billions?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260421_2_notedejes.Vl1uvf&refcode=em20260421-962&amount=5&t=1&akid=962%2E299639%2EyoKRKw)
I grew up in Brownsville public schools — schools where no one had much, but we had each other.
That’s where I learned that doing right by others isn’t charity — **it’s duty.**
It’s why I also became a lawyer, so I can fight for workers and families just like my parents did. And when my son’s elementary school — steps from the Capitol — was threatened with closure, I ran for the Austin school board. We stopped a corporate takeover of our public schools and kept every single campus open. Our schools passed accountability standards for the first time in history.
A few years later, I ran for the Texas House to keep fighting for our kids and our classrooms. Since then, I’ve:
✅ Passed a first-of-its-kind law creating Public Benefit Corporations so Texas businesses can do well and do good.
✅ Secured nearly a billion dollars in federal funds for health care in Travis County.
✅ Led the charge to stop Abbott’s voucher scams and defend public schools — beating him five times in a row.
✅ Helped organize the Democratic walkout that blocked Abbott’s voter suppression bill and protected Texans’ right to vote.
Every fight has reinforced what my grandmother taught me. I can still hear her voice every time I wear the ring she gave me before she passed: No te dejes.
**Never back down.**
Greg Abbott’s corruption runs deep, and the billionaires he serves will spend whatever it takes to keep him in power. But I’ve beaten him before — and with your help, I’ll do it again.
If you believe in a Texas where every child can learn in a great public school, where families can afford healthcare, where every worker can earn a living wage, and where the government serves the people, not the powerful, _then I need you in this fight from day one._
**[Peter, if you’re with me, will you donate $5 to my campaign today?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260421_2_notedejes.Vl1uvf&refcode=em20260421-962&amount=5&t=2&akid=962%2E299639%2EyoKRKw)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260421_2_notedejes.Vl1uvf&amount=5&refcode=em20260421-962&t=21&akid=962%2E299639%2EyoKRKw)
**We can do this. We’re Texans.** We do hard things — and we’ve never been afraid of a fight.
_No te dejes._
With gratitude and determination,
Gina Hinojosa

name: Mallory McMorrow
subject: Saving the USPS and our elections
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McMorrow for Michigan
body:
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4523%2E898137%2EZIlYQV)
Trump and his administration are trying to dismantle the USPS and limit how people can vote.
During Donald Trump’s first term, he made Louis DeJoy — a major GOP donor — the Postmaster General. DeJoy increased costs, cut staff, slowed down delivery times, and got in the way of people voting by mail.
(By the way, DeJoy is a major donor to my MAGA opponent Mike Rogers.)
Donald Trump is continuing his attacks on the postal service, and he recently signed an executive order trying to limit mail-in voting — even though he, Melania, and his kids just voted by mail. Seriously.
This is yet another attempt from Trump to take over elections from states, so he can put his orange thumb on the scale in the races he cares about.
Here in Michigan, our elections are secure and have high turnout because people have so many ways to cast their ballots. We've led the nation in expanding access to and securing our right to vote, and we won't stop now.
As Senator, I'll work to protect voting rights and vote by mail so all voters have equitable access to the ballot. But with people like Louis DeJoy backing Mike Rogers, I think it’s safe to say Rogers won’t be a champion for voting rights.
[**If you’re on board with my pro-voter, pro-democracy plans, will you sign on as an endorser of my campaign for Senate?**](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-202604-Endorse-vbm?refcode=AU_MAM_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260421_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=4523%2E898137%2EZIlYQV)
| [SIGN ON](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/signup/MAM-202604-Endorse-vbm?refcode=AU_MAM_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260421_PM1_V1_S1&t=3&akid=4523%2E898137%2EZIlYQV)
---
This is a fight we can win together — for Michigan and for every voter who deserves an easy, secure path to the ballot.
Thank you for showing up.
– Mallory

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Peter, **This morning, I convened a shadow hearing on taxing corporate greed because working people deserve leaders who are willing not only to name the problem but to fight to fix it too**. Because here’s what we all know: working people are doing everything right, and still getting squeezed and told to tighten their belts. Families are paying more at the grocery store, more for housing, more for health care — while billionaires and massive corporations rake in record profits and use a rigged tax code to avoid paying their fair share. [_**So, I wanted to reach out personally, right after this morning’s hearing, because this fight is just too important not to. If you’re able, will you click here and chip in ANY AMOUNT to help me keep using every tool available to take on corporate greed?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129911759/615965788/-522603630?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YTJhZDYwNS1kMTNkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VVkL3F6pPNVvgA1SJMAOZTv9eSJe0hAbKuLHUUBX15g=) I did not come to Congress to sit back and wait for somebody else to take this on. **I came here to fight like hell to unrig this system and make life more affordable for the people who are working hard every single day just to get by**. Friend, I have some big news. I’m launching something new, and I want you to be a part of it from the jump. I grew up in the kind of small town where everybody knew everybody, everybody’s kids played together, and everybody helped when someone was in trouble. We used to gather together as neighbors to celebrate after football games and graduations. More often than not, our gatherings took place at our local public school. My public school was foundational. It was more than my education and the name on my jersey: it was the place our town came to meet. _Heck, the school was the town. _ As I’ve visited small towns in other states over the years, I’ve witnessed a similar sentiment. In red districts and blue, I’ve heard about cherished local schools and how they serve as the cornerstones of their communities. But nowadays I’m seeing a disturbing new trend as those cornerstones are starting to crumble: **Local schools are closing after funding cuts, and they’re followed by other foundational pieces of the community. ** The local grocery store? Gone. The local clinic? _Gone._ The job with a decent wage? _Gone._ Everyone and everything seems to be packing up and leaving town. We’re losing our neighbors. We’re losing our communities. And we aren't talking to each other anymore. This is what it looks like to defund and divide America, and it’s because of Republicans like Donald Trump and JD Vance, who are willing to sell out our communities and working families for their own political and financial gain. Why is Elon Musk closing schools in America? Why are we being told that any of the hardships our communities are facing have to do with immigration? The problem isn't your neighbor. It’s the tech bros and billionaires who pay to take turns cosplaying as your Congressman, your Senator, and your President. I think folks in small towns need to band together and stand up for our schools, our jobs, and our communities before they’re all gone. **It’s time to put the power back into the hands of our neighbors, and for Democrats to expand the map. That’s why I’m excited to launch Small Town PAC.** I’m ready to pass the baton and get out on the road to find some teachers, some nurses, some veterans, laborers, and young people in small towns across the country who can represent their communities better than Silicon Valley and corrupt Republicans. We need a new generation of elected leaders in this country – and lord knows the Democrats need some new faces. So let’s go recruit some good people with energy and ideas who actually understand small towns and are willing to fight for them. clean_body: | | Friend, I have some big news. I’m launching something new, and I want you to be a part of it from the jump. I grew up in the kind of small town where everybody knew everybody, everybody’s kids played together, and everybody helped when someone was in trouble. We used to gather together as neighbors to celebrate after football games and graduations. More often than not, our gatherings took place at our local public school. My public school was foundational. It was more than my education and the name on my jersey: it was the place our town came to meet. Heck, the school was the town. As I’ve visited small towns in other states over the years, I’ve witnessed a similar sentiment. In red districts and blue, I’ve heard about cherished local schools and how they serve as the cornerstones of their communities. But nowadays I’m seeing a disturbing new trend as those cornerstones are starting to crumble: Local schools are closing after funding cuts, and they’re followed by other foundational pieces of the community. The local grocery store? Gone. The local clinic? Gone. The job with a decent wage? Gone. Everyone and everything seems to be packing up and leaving town. We’re losing our neighbors. We’re losing our communities. And we aren't talking to each other anymore. This is what it looks like to defund and divide America, and it’s because of Republicans like Donald Trump and JD Vance, who are willing to sell out our communities and working families for their own political and financial gain. Why is Elon Musk closing schools in America? Why are we being told that any of the hardships our communities are facing have to do with immigration? The problem isn't your neighbor. It’s the tech bros and billionaires who pay to take turns cosplaying as your Congressman, your Senator, and your President. I think folks in small towns need to band together and stand up for our schools, our jobs, and our communities before they’re all gone. It’s time to put the power back into the hands of our neighbors, and for Democrats to expand the map. That’s why I’m excited to launch Small Town PAC. I’m ready to pass the baton and get out on the road to find some teachers, some nurses, some veterans, laborers, and young people in small towns across the country who can represent their communities better than Silicon Valley and corrupt Republicans. We need a new generation of elected leaders in this country – and lord knows the Democrats need some new faces. So let’s go recruit some good people with energy and ideas who actually understand small towns and are willing to fight for them. We’re on a mission to build a party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately. _**By David Shuster**_
American capitalism has long been exceptionally greedy. Rapaciousness, after all, is as old as commerce itself. But in the United States under Trump, even the faintest pretense of embarrassment has been obliterated. What was once done with a wink is now performed with a trumpet.
Consider the latest performance at the Magic Kingdom. The newly anointed chief executive officer of the Walt Disney company, Josh D'Amaro, has been awarded a compensation package worth $45 million a year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

At the same time, D'Amaro just signed off on the firing of 1,000 company employees, as if they were defective bolts rattling loose on Space Mountain.
Disney leadership is speaking solemnly about "efficiencies," the most elastic of modern corporate euphemisms.
But let's not stop there. Disney has contrived, by perfectly legal means, to pay an effective federal income tax rate of zero. Zero! It is a figure that would have astonished even the most creative accountants of the Gilded Age. Meanwhile, Disney last year accepted 4.7 billion dollars in U.S. government rebates--public money, extracted from the very citizenry now asked to applaud the firings and layoffs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

And now, to reassure analysts and investors on Wall Street that Disney's relatively anemic stock performance is getting a boost, Disney is planning to spend $7 billion buying back its own stock. The chief virtue of this maneuver will be to inflate Disney stock prices, further lifting the fortunes of Disney stockholders and executives.
If this is not greed, then the word has lost all meaning.
Conservative corporate apologists, of course, are already clearing their throats. They insist, with the enthusiasm of Maurice from Beauty and the Beast instructing his daughter Belle, that each of these acts is defensible in isolation.

The pay is "performance based." The layoffs are "strategic." The taxes are "optimized." The buybacks are "value-enhancing." Thus Disney, like other modern corporations, gets to disassemble its conduct into a series of bloodless abstractions, each scrubbed clean of consequence.
But many Americans, despite our nation's embrace of obscene individual and corporate greed, still have the vulgar habit of considering the whole of our society. And we can see that at Disney and countless other corporate icons, the game has been rigged. The winnings flow upwards, the losses downward, and the Disney financiers and speculators congratulate themselves on their skills and dexterity.
Ironically, there was once was a time in America, improbable as it now sounds, when captains of industry exhibited some restraint. Take Mitt Romney's father George Romney, who ran American Motors in an era when the word "millionaire" still retained a whiff of astonishment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Romney voluntarily declined $268,000 in pay over five years--roughly a fifth of what he might have taken--and in 1960 refused a $100,000 bonus on the grounds that it would push him above a self-imposed ceiling of $225,000. He had previously informed his board, in a fit of what today would be diagnosed as moral derangement, that no executive needed to earn more than that.
George Romney was no monk. He lived well, ate well, and doubtless slept soundly. But he labored under the conviction that there existed some relationship--however tenuous--between what corporate leaders took for themselves and the general health of the society around them.
Such thinking has since been annihilated.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

At the Magic Kingdom, and throughout American capitalism, we have erected and embraced a system in which excess is not just tolerated but celebrated, in which the ability to extract the maximum possible sum is regarded as a mark of genius, and in which any appeal to proportion or fairness is dismissed as the whining of the liberal left.
And it's not just about CEO pay, worker layoffs, and obscene corporate tax rates. Most Americans who have visited Disney World in recent years will tell you that the park has become exceptionally expensive. A Mickey's Chocolate Covered Ice Cream Bar now costs $6.50 each. That's more than twice the price from 15 years ago and far exceeds the rate of inflation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

A Mickey pretzel has gone up by 118% and now costs $8.25. And never mind giving your kid a soft pretzel or ice cream treat, a basic "Mickey Ears hat" has also soared well beyond inflation. 15 years ago, it was $11.95. Now, the mouse hat will set you back $20 plus taxes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Just getting into the theme park has also outpaced inflation. Over the past ten years, the price of admission has doubled.
The price gouging and corporate profit taking at Disney is obscene. And this similar corporate strategy across America has a long term cost on our basic humanity. The U.S. labor force is perpetually on edge. The U.S. treasury keeps being treated as a trough for the billionaire class. And the gulf is getting wider between those who make governmental and business decisions and those who endure them.
Trust, that fragile and necessary lubricant of any functioning society, is evaporating. Cynicism is rushing in to take its place.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c29cb9c4-9227-42a4-a950-0333b96b628b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The answer, delivered with rehearsed jubilation, is always the same: "I'm going to Disney World."
Today, in this era of unabashed greed, the question and answer should be altered. "Corporate CEO, you've just shed a thousand workers, paid no taxes, and secured yourself a king's ransom--where are you going next?" The answer, stripped of its confetti, would be just as predictable: "straight to the bank, by way of Disney World."

| | , Since launching this campaign last September, I’ve been dreaming of how we could make politics feel joyful at a time where the world feels like it’s on fire. Much to the establishment’s chagrin, block parties, battle of the bands, karaoke nights, and concerts have always been part of our strategy. This weekend, joy was on full display. Saturday’s [Benefit Concert](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/9wKJ7tqDe3rV1PCEUln1iA~~/AAUS1hA~/P0nZe0OvHNI-UOb6x1HcBfQBre_rvzf3cL3QDYqPsD6RHbonb6wlM-NW644MOZSht4ADMD_XqXX8VF-YRIZw9Xn2S9Wr9vVL7RvRgpXu9zGZtWrGg97hgzTbKVtNOvoCICvMDCzHSHiagULaB6wyjw~~) happened because a campaign supporter had a band, an idea, and a community they brought in to support them. They were joined by another full band, multiple solo musicians, and even launched a new song, _Put Hope to Work,_ written by a few people very dear to my heart,__ that’ll be on repeat as soon as it’s released (stay tuned). This event wasn’t just for the 100+ locals who came to what one couple described as a “social safe place,” where they trusted the community enough to let their guard down. It also drew two people from Michigan who, on the invitation from a local supporter, drove 16 hours in a weekend to experience the energy firsthand. For me, hosting events isn’t just a fundraising tactic — though y’all helped us raise more than $5,000 this weekend! — it’s a promise I made when I entered this race that I would do things differently for the sake of a different result. The same old political playbook of stump speeches and plated dinners isn’t what will bring this movement all the way to D.C. Joy? Community? Belonging? Hope? I have a hunch that will give us momentum to November and beyond. We’re especially excited about our [party at The Lighthouse in Knoxville](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/gWMV3VBWZ9j9MnCCiTu7ow~~/AAUS1hA~/H14NgT_o4lXdKC2vxerw2ypnli_6ZkFh5VJ4d-cpJ2XKGRTzhGOKUyyuTt-WfQmNi0rofALH0SwA_k5Txy7qmai8pS2t2Ns1BdLFjPAelq0uRTvAQ-0GqmqzF4uC121ijUWZNu5IVwmPBmWQ5k6LwVYqxRP6_TEewL5Wfaoi3XU~) on April 29. clean_body: The next two weeks are STACKED with events! | | | , Since launching this campaign last September, I’ve been dreaming of how we could make politics feel joyful at a time where the world feels like it’s on fire. Much to the establishment’s chagrin, block parties, battle of the bands, karaoke nights, and concerts have always been part of our strategy. This weekend, joy was on full display. Saturday’s ~~ happened because a campaign supporter had a band, an idea, and a community they brought in to support them. They were joined by another full band, multiple solo musicians, and even launched a new song, Put Hope to Work, written by a few people very dear to my heart, that’ll be on repeat as soon as it’s released (stay tuned). This event wasn’t just for the 100+ locals who came to what one couple described as a “social safe place,” where they trusted the community enough to let their guard down. It also drew two people from Michigan who, on the invitation from a local supporter, drove 16 hours in a weekend to experience the energy firsthand. For me, hosting events isn’t just a fundraising tactic — though y’all helped us raise more than $5,000 this weekend! — it’s a promise I made when I entered this race that I would do things differently for the sake of a different result. The same old political playbook of stump speeches and plated dinners isn’t what will bring this movement all the way to D.C. Joy? Community? Belonging? Hope? I have a hunch that will give us momentum to November and beyond. We’re especially excited about our ~ on April 29. Bring a friend or two (and your youngsters — there will be a kids activity!) and hear my plans for how this movement is working for a better East Tennessee. With gratitude, Michaela Upcoming events you won't want to miss: April 22 — ~: We'll walk through our voter outreach program and share all the ways you can get involved in flipping TN-02. April 26 — ~~ : Join the Loudon Dems and special guest Tim Wise at their annual fundraiser. Peter,

Trump unleashed ICE into Minnesota — and the results were devastating.
Communities torn apart, families separated, neighborhoods destroyed, and
innocent lives lost. The trauma and fear left behind are still felt today.

Now, a former ICE prosecutor is running to challenge Ilhan’s seat. It’s a
direct threat to the leaders who have fought tirelessly for our
communities, our rights, and our future.

Someone who was part of a system that caused so much harm wants to take
the place of a champion who has stood up for justice, equality, and
safety.

We cannot allow that to happen — we deserve leaders who fight for us, not
against us. Leaders who prioritize protecting families over punishing
them. Leaders who invest in solutions that build stronger neighborhoods
rather than tearing them down.

Ilhan is that leader, and now it’s up to us to ensure she stays in
Congress.

The Squad Victory Fund is mobilizing to protect her seat. We’re
organizing, reaching voters, and building the grassroots power necessary
to fight back against candidates who represent fear, division, and
destruction. But we can’t do it without you.

Our campaign was a grassroots one, and it’s because of YOU that our team was able to compete with the MAGA dark money and billionaire-funded NO campaign.

No matter what happens we’re proud of how we showed up and left it all on the table.
Thank you for your support,
Virginians For Fair Elections

subject: We need to end these reckless foreign wars
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1304%2E1086043%2ETBWGXb)
Peter,
Gas prices are up over $4. Medicare, Medicaid, and child care are on the chopping block. **_But the President and his lackeys are distracted by the forever war they started._**
I served in the military, and I know that force should always be the last resort. A mission must be clear. The war in Iran is not meeting that standard — _and the American people are the ones reaping the consequences._
I won’t let Donald Trump’s chaos stand in the way of progress in Maryland. We’re still laser focused on lowering costs on everything from energy to groceries, creating affordable housing, and protecting health care. In fact, we just invested a historic amount to make childcare more affordable for Maryland families.
**[I need you with me to continue this progress. Our re-election effort is powered by grassroots supporters like you, Peter, so I have to ask: Can you chip in $5 today to help us keep delivering for Marylanders?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260421-1.OkSHFQ&refcode=em-20260421-1&t=2&akid=1304%2E1086043%2ETBWGXb)**

Peace and love, everyone! This is your forever congressman, Jamaal Bowman. I am proud and honored to support Adem Bunkeddeko for New York State Comptroller.
The Democratic primary is coming up fast — early voting runs June 13 through June 21, with Election Day on June 23. It is time to elect a progressive champion to this critically important office.
Learn more about Adem and his vision at the link below, and please chip in to help push him over the finish line → [HERE](https://ademfornewyork.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=81a9f685946c3d17fe402b3fb&id=71c5c3db6e&e=5702859c35)
The Comptroller wields tremendous power over how New York State invests its money. When we elect Adem, he will work to make New York more affordable by building affordable housing and investing in our children. Adem will also divest from war and hold Wall Street accountable, while reinvesting in the working-class people of New York.
-Jamaal Bowman
