Iran Talks in Freefall

The U.S.-Iran ceasefire is on life support. President Trump [said Tuesday](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O6yAQhZ8Gd46YMbZJQXEbd7ntltYEhgRl_CMg8euvvPsGWx_pO985X7f5RknS-vhPC7tc4xy2MKdMayV5lZiZI4kclMszkp9R49Bq0yLMq8zYBBd8IPANOxjHwYLpoWuebvSaIfSxt9R5HRgQ7LXD6x0skba-Se5EaYOAXdeDvpjBGOD7MFiN1nBQRpNwrpfM-_suyZ9K5RW37Pnit6UR96x1L6r7p3BSONG-8lHOSOEk6cMKp3NIe1BuU8nE0tb8XvZf__bsb7IL-5FEUhlGZfRjoSQ_9PqHMz4OvwMAAP__CgxsjQ) that extending the truce is "highly unlikely" and that the U.S. military is "raring to go" for resumed strikes--a deliberate signal to Tehran as the deadline closes in. The U.S. seized an Iranian oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz as Vice President Vance headed to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks. Iran's Foreign Ministry signaled it [does not plan to reengage](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD3O5CAMQE-TdEQYGJIUFNukm223jBwwEzTkR0AGaU-_ykh7ga-z_CTrPf95zk8MMeyv37iRScXP7nBzSLgXjO_sE5HHGCumvHq0s-BCM66YgHmPs2idcdYh2JYM9L0eQD1AtqvpcfTejpxLUOB1D_pBIKV3vbXjIKEN5j7FlQAh5QN4p7RSQIvWAxeDItcojpFS6RKd1xKDvZXy2x_JUmePrY1mLeXMjfzViKkRU6212xe7U803vzdHiq4R053TiCmGD7ElHq__83U6LJTZzVnFxEq6tpOdhJbYt599cLfELGEmHxKxvIaTrUfarr8s2R2lAlBjm4w7a4gxZN03ir82DPErWX7w048R_wIAAP__xUGHiw) "for now," leaving the Islamabad talks in doubt before they begin. The standoff is increasingly binary: Iran agrees to structured talks on its nuclear program, or the bombs fall again. Trump has set the terms. The Strait of Hormuz seizure--affecting roughly [20% of global oil flow](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1uwzAQg5_G3mRIZ0VOBg1dvKVrR-Msn-JD5B-clLjo0xfuI3QkSBAf-XUf7siJ18cnLuSlxGHapoEF14LpmaMQRUzpQMlzxDCABqe0VWCGNQ1QT34KE5pQkzdd567GXkxbz_7SgjbB3UaKo7lRN7oAaG7RRqfRdaZmf1ZpCwba9mJ0Y521hkbnrhqulqbKakwkpRHaX2PicCLlZ9wkUBO2pU5-LmXPVftRQV9BfxxHE7fvlY58-hX0id-kTl1Bf05SB4oq8lp2lYsgFzVvsrx-VCDMFFnO9GMrjIW3Nasdn5wLrgp34aTA1OKn_eCUOLuusvqxIKc_mPKP794efgMAAP__d5GA0Q)--is leverage, not escalation, in the White House's framing. ★★★
Warsh Faces Senate Fire

Kevin Warsh's path to the Federal Reserve chairmanship got rockier Tuesday. The Senate Banking Committee subjected Trump's nominee to hours of cross-examination on Fed independence, with Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., [calling him Trump's "sock puppet"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2O7CAQhE-DMyxoY2wHBC9xNi_d0GpDM4MG_wiY5for9gibdfCp66v6emwPDDGcz_94kEnFb-5yW0h4Fozv7BORxxgrpvzyaDcQoLlQHOR2xg06Z5x1KG1HRk6TnqUa5dC9zOSXaSa7LIPDHcHJEXbtJM16VE5q6IJpr4QCCcMwStErrZSkXetZwKzIMSUwUip9ovuzx2CbUn77K1nq7XV00bxKuTMb_jFYGay11v6-YijBXg1gsJ5UM4O1JTFYhWq3bGirwyumRCfPdGIh7snxkj7HzRMWytyFbOOVP4m4EPM8THLpknF3DTGGrCemxPPAEH9dyh-m-zbwEwAA___HmXwM)--a charge Warsh flatly denied. Warsh pushed back hard: "I will not be a sock puppet for anyone." But the hearing exposed the political complexity of his position. Several Republican senators [signaled reservations](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOgzAQRL_GdEb2YhyucHENXa69Ei32OlhZDDJO-P0T-YTrRhrp6c383qc7Jk758YMruVLjFLYwpYK5Ij-PWIgiMp9YjiWin0CBlcpI0FPmCZrggg-ofUNO32520KbXXbM4Y20_2xkUQq9NiN1X38EcKXjTa1RDk9yFUgY0dF2vVWusMZpmawcFg6EgjEKmUttC-2vm5C-l4xm34qn129qwW2rdD9F9CxgFjOd5tj7P_ioFjBdewKjMlbWA8UnvlOVniYwUpN9yTGXFmrYsF8KS8kPW8lp3yelN8rUHrHS0S125KS7sZ2JOh70Jox4rJv5Y1H-c9nbwFwAA___cRnsa) about past statements and his extensive financial holdings--raising real questions about whether 50 votes are there. The confirmation battle tracks a deeper anxiety inside the GOP: Trump wants a Fed chairman who will cut rates on demand, and Congress is being asked to ratify someone claiming he won't. The committee vote timeline is unclear. If even two Republicans peel off, Warsh's confirmation [could stall](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOhCAQhp9GOwwgoltQXGO3115pRhhW4ggGuN3s21_cR7hukvny5_v_n_tyh0AhPr7hQJOrX1xyS8gQK9BefEb0QPSCXDYPdpFcasYVk2KJtMjWGWcdCNuiEeOoJ6EG0bebAVjteOPc4sidmNQ69Nh7LUZQQg_Wt8FcUVxJIft-ELxTWimBq9YTl5NC1ygOhLl2Gc_flYK9lMruU7bY2XS0ZLZaz9L0X42cGzn7ECFa7N6wpXQRjZzRppiOdyPnM1Gw10HhiReNjtkUfcgH1JAi2xByiA92_dmOzxDZpzXzYLGwghEqMoLXATvmwqRQk-hvXHRbPajNxp2vQBSKHhvFHwcE-mjWf6z6NPIvAAD__1mmiGA) before reaching the floor. ★★★
Third Cabinet Seat Empties

Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer resigned Monday amid an internal misconduct investigation--becoming the third member of Trump's Cabinet to step down in his second term, and the third woman. The former one-term Oregon congresswoman [faced multiple allegations](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L1ygzAQBOCnEZ0Y6ZAELlSkoXPalMwhHUZj8TOHbJI8fcZ-hHRbfbuzX9fhiimn9faJC3ku0xC3OCTGtWC-HxMTTZjziXzME4YBFDipjAQ9rHmAKvoYIupQkddt6zptrG6q2cfOWjuFEfVlCnRBsNE5a9qmAVQYoEr-RSkDGprGalUbZ4ym0blOQWcoCqMwE5eaaX-MOYXXpOM-bRyoDttSZT-Xsh-i-RDQC-jP86zXneuNbwL6ly6gV-adBfTrtzy0tG1zAasF9BnHjeVBgakg_8jCj2WXYcYn_cpITAtxxT7uZ8o5Ha4VRt0WTPldXv7x1dPDXwAAAP___Y92Fg) including an affair with a subordinate and drinking on the job. Chavez-DeRemer follows the firings of Kristi Noem (Homeland Security) and Pam Bondi (Attorney General) earlier in the term. Three departures in roughly 90 days of a second-term administration is not normal turnover--it's a pattern. The White House [has yet to name a replacement](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOtCAUhZ8GOw1cEf0Lir-hm223NFe4jGQQDTCa7NNvnEfY7hQn5zv5vh_zA0MM6fmFG-lc_ex2N4eMqWJ8FZ-JPMZ4YS6rRzsDB9Vy2YKYU5yhcdpZh8I2pMU4qknIQfTNqglH6gdJJAYgO5Hn1jqw4h8q9IC-Cfqe4hIE9P0geCeVlIIWpSYOkyTHJMdIuXaZjvcSg70vlZffs6XO7lsT9VrrUVj_n4FhYK7r6i4sa0jPuqdjL_WuMTDLu4REpTAwN5OB4fKTGRi74kk_raNMG-U2Ep5UWotLSFQZmCZrd1whxlDUyCR_bhjiB1__YOvU8BsAAP__Jt15dQ). The Department of Labor (DOL) is now running without a Senate-confirmed secretary heading into a politically sensitive midterm stretch--a management vulnerability that Democrats will exploit. [Republicans on the Hill](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLvOnDAQRp_GdEb2YC6NizR0mzYlGuxhsXa4aOxdlDx9xD7C333SJx0dnT-P6YGJ0_78jRt5KcsUjzglwb0gv_IiRAsyXyh5XTBMYKDTxmmw084TVNHHENGGirzt-26wrrVNtfoBY48d4mIDQmzbwZpmgRmR-sY281Alf6OMAwtN01pTu845S3PXDQYGR1E5g0xSaqHzPXMKt1J-LYcEqsOxVezXUs6sml8KRgXjdV112Pf7UzDedAWjcd-tYDwPTiWFrGDkQ5IOK37on44ktJFoxvkQnSkIFZS_-ngXXeS9nZX4eF6JOeWuV848N0z8FSg_6PXx8D8AAP__Hfx5xQ) are privately raising concerns about the nomination and vetting pipeline.

I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.

_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.

That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**P.S.** Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture.

But moments like this don't sustain themselves.

If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple.

**We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. **

clean_body: This is the part most people don’t see | | | | | Friend, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. And we don't take that lightly. I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture. But moments like this don't sustain themselves. If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple. We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day. If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

Hello, I want to share something that happened recently.
A man reached out to me out of the blue. He said, “I’ve been a lifelong Republican. I’m a soybean farmer.”
He told me he had four questions and asked if we could talk. I said, of course. We got on the phone. He asked me his first question. Then his second.
After I answered, he paused and said, “Where can I send you $1,000?”
That stuck with me because this isn’t about party labels anymore. It’s about people who feel like no one is listening to them.
Will you join him and chip in $5, $15, $50 — whatever you can? It’ll go toward town halls, flyers, gas, and the real, on-the-ground work it takes to win. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2604-q2-ak]
DONATE → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2604-q2-ak]
Here in Colorado’s 3rd District, people are done with Jeff Hurd enabling bad Trump policies that raise costs, threaten healthcare, and ignore the needs of our communities.
I’ve spent the last year traveling across all 27 counties, meeting people where they are, listening to their concerns, and fighting for real solutions.
And I’m hearing it everywhere that people want leadership that shows up—and actually works for them. If you believe it’s time for something different, I’m asking you to join us. Donate today. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2604-q2-ak]

Together, we can show that this movement is bigger than politics.
